units.english_text: *After the candles on the main Holy Table are lit and two censers prepared, if two deacons are to serve (if not, then one), the Priest, having blessed the epitrachelion with his hand arranged as for the blessing at Liturgy and having kissed the cross upon it, puts it on himself[^6]. The deacons take upon themselves the sticharion with the orarion, having kissed it beforehand. All three come out, one after another—first the second deacon, after him the first, and last the Priest—from the sacristy to the front of the steps of the Holy Table. Having taken their stand: the first deacon on the left, and the second on the right of the Priest, with the Priest between them, all three bow low to the Holy Mysteries and, having turned all together to the Holy Doors (the Priest and second deacon to the right, and the first deacon to the left), they open them and, having turned toward the Holy Table, likewise by a half-turn, the deacons take the censers, and the Priest, with his right hand, takes the spoon and puts incense first into the censer of the first, and then into the censer of the second deacon. And after the deacons say:*

units.english_text: *At this time, all rise; the deacons cense, always with three swings of the censer, first the Holy Table from the four sides—namely first from the front both together, bowing low to the Holy Mysteries while doing so; then the first deacon goes to the right side, and the second to the left, each censing his own side of the Holy Table, and also from behind (and, if it exists, the icon behind the Holy Table) both together, and they cense the Priest from the front corners of the Holy Table both together, and come out, each through his own door, to the front of the Holy Doors and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, they turn to the local icons of the iconostasis, each censing the icon on his own side. Also, they go around the temple with smoking censers, each on his own side, censing while doing so the icons of the side altars, if such exist. After this, having returned from the great church doors through the middle of the temple to the front of the Holy Doors and having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, they turn—the Deacon who is on the right to the left, and the Deacon who is on the left to the right—toward the west, and each censes the kliros on his own side (if the church is a cathedral, also the choirs) and, at the end, both together cense the people.*

units.english_text: Six troparia are taken: first of the Temple (if dedicated to the Lord or the Theotokos), then the troparion of the weekday. If the Temple is dedicated to a Saint, then first the troparion of the day, and after it of the Temple; followed by the four troparia in the *Horologion* beginning with "O God of our Fathers." (On Thursday, having a double commemoration, there are 7 troparia, and in monasteries 8 with St. Basil[^20]. On Wednesday and Friday, the Cross troparion "O Lord, save Thy people" always takes first place).

units.english_text: * **On Sundays:** Kathisma 17 is read throughout most of the year. The 19th Kathisma (Polyeleos—Psalms 134 and 135) is sung on Sundays from the Apodosis of the Holy Cross (September 22) to the Forefeast of the Nativity (December 19), and from the Apodosis of Theophany (January 14) to Cheesefare Sunday. After it follow the Resurrectional Evlogitaria ("The Angelic Host"), Small Litany, and the Hypakoe of the tone.

units.english_text: 1. **Single Commemoration:** If there is only one troparion, it is taken with "**Glory:**", followed by "**Both now:**" and the Theotokion of the Hour. If there are two troparia and two kontakia, the first troparion is taken simply, the second with "**Glory:**", followed by "**Both now:**" and the Theotokion of the Hour. The kontakia are taken alternately: at the 1st and 6th Hours—the first; at the 3rd and 9th Hours—the second.

units.english_text: * *Polyeleos / Kathisma 17:* Kathisma 17 (*“The Blameless”*) or Kathisma 19 (Polyeleos). Kathisma 17 is read on Sundays between the Apodosis of the Holy Cross (September 21) and the Forefeast of the Nativity (December 20); Kathisma 19 is sung on Sundays between the Apodosis of Theophany (January 14) and the 1st Sunday of Great Lent[^57]. After Kathisma 17 or 19: immediately the Resurrectional Evlogitaria (*“The Angelic Host”*), Small Litany, and the Hypakoe of the current tone.

units.english_text: This Saturday and Sunday have nothing in the church service, except the Prokimenon-Alleluia and Apostle-Gospel at the Liturgy. However, since it may fall during the Forefeast, on the Feast, during the Afterfeast and on the Apodosis of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, [and] during the Afterfeast of the Exaltation of the Precious Cross, we give the rule for all five cases, first for the Saturday, and afterwards for the Sunday.

provenance.verbatim_source: This Saturday and Sunday have nothing in the church service, except the Prokimenon-Alleluia and Apostle-Gospel at the Liturgy. However, since it may fall during the Forefeast, on the Feast, during the Afterfeast and on the Apodosis of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, [and] during the Afterfeast of the Exaltation of the Precious Cross, we give the rule for all five cases, first for the Saturday, and afterwards for the Sunday.

units.english_text: The service of this feast is celebrated according to the general rule of Great Feasts of the Lord. However, it differs from other feasts in that on this feast the Bringing Out, Exaltation of the precious Cross and Veneration of it takes place. The Bringing Out from the sacristy to the mensa takes place in the Eve of the feast, after the dismissal of Small Vespers, or if there is none, then before the beginning of Great Vespers. From the mensa to the tetrapod – on the very day of the feast at Matins, during the Great Doxology. The Exaltation (Vozdvyzhennia) takes place on the tetrapod after the Great Doxology. The Veneration – immediately after the Exaltation and after every service celebrated in the church until the Apodosis of the feast (21 September). All this happens as presented below, first of all – the preparation of the precious Cross.

units.english_text: The Priest, having entered the sacristy, takes the aer from the chalice, spreads it on the Table of Oblation (Proskomedia), with the reverse side to the altar, and the face side – to himself; then he takes basil with his left hand (if there is none, then other fragrant herbs) and places them on the Precious Cross, ties it to them with a ribbon (band) and, placing the face side to the aer, wraps it together with the basil with that aer from all sides and, having wrapped the aer from all sides at the bottom, ties it firmly with another ribbon to the Cross: from the middle to the bottom of the Cross. Then he takes the Cross wrapped in this way with his left [hand], folds the aer with his right hand from the top to the bottom so that the Precious Cross and the face side of the aer are visible from the middle of the Cross and lower; finally he takes the diskos from the chalice and places it under the top of the Cross, between the basil and the Cross[^259].

units.english_text: After the dismissal of Small Vespers, or where there is none, then before the beginning of Great [Vespers], the Priest, wearing an epitrachelion[^260], the Deacon, if there be one, – a dalmatic with an orarion of crimson color, according to the Lviv Synod, violet, stand before the Table of Oblation, where the precious Cross lies with basil branches, and behind him stand two candle-bearers with lit candles. The Deacon censes the precious Cross and says: "Bless, Master", the Priest begins: "Blessed is our God". If there be no deacon, the Priest, having censed himself, exclaims: "Blessed is our God". Choir: "Amen", also Trisagion and the rest with "Our Father". Priest: "For Thine is the kingdom". After this the Choir sings the Troparion "Save, O Lord", Glory, Both now: Kontakion "Thou Who Wast lifted up" ("voznesyisya").

units.english_text: The Priest, having bowed to the precious Cross, takes it with both hands and, having rested it on his head on that side where the basil is, turns and, preceded by two candle-bearers and accompanied on the right side by the Deacon who censes the precious Cross, exits the sacristy. The candle-bearers and the Deacon stand before the steps of the altar near the Holy Doors, and the Priest approaches the Holy Table, "lays the precious Cross on the holy mensa, in the place of the holy Gospel[^261], and places the Gospel on the High Place (that is near the tabernacle, opposite himself) and a candle is lit before it for the whole night"[^262]. At the end the Priest with the concelebrants bows and withdraws behind the candle-bearers and behind the Deacon to the sacristy[^263].

units.english_text: TRANSFER. When the stichera of the Praises are sung, the Priest with the Deacon or deacons, if there be [any], withdraw to the sacristy and vest in all sacred vestments of their rank of crimson color, according to the Lviv Synod, violet, exactly as for the Liturgy. At the end of the stichera they go before the steps of the altar and, having bowed low, open the Holy Doors. The Priest exclaims: "Glory to Thee, Who Hast shown us the light". The choirs sing the Great Doxology, and the Priest goes out through the Holy Doors to the tetrapod, takes the Gospel and carries it to the Holy Table. Having taken the censer, he censes the precious Cross crosswise three times, gives the censer to the Deacon and, having bowed low, takes the precious Cross with both hands and, having rested it on his head, basil to himself, Cross to the people, goes out before the steps and, preceded by two candle-bearers and the Deacon with the censer, goes around the altar from its right side, makes an entrance through the northern doors and stands before the Holy Doors between the deacons and behind the candle-bearers and there awaits the end of the Doxology and Trisagion. At their end the Deacon, and if there is none, then the Priest himself loudly exclaims: "Wisdom, attend!". Then they turn, go before the tetrapod by the right side: first the candle-bearers, behind them – the Deacon with the censer, and at the end – the Priest. The Priest places the precious Cross on a pillow at the top of the tetrapod, covered with a tablecloth or a costly covering, censes it from four sides, and the choirs sing the Troparion "Save, O Lord"[^264].

units.english_text: EXALTATION: After the singing of the Troparion and censing of the Precious Cross, the Priest takes the precious Cross with both hands and, standing before the tetrapod, facing east, sings[^265] solemnly and joyfully the first petition of the litany "Have mercy on us, O God". Then, having signed with the precious Cross three times crosswise to the east, He begins to slowly bow His head to the ground, as much as possible (according to the rule – so that the head is a span away from the ground"). The Choir begins to sing in a quiet and humble voice, according to the rule, the first hundred, according to the present [custom], eight triplets, that is 24 "Lord, have mercy", lowering the voice with each triplet until it finishes the fourth triplet, then it raises the voice with each of the three following triplets, and the Priest gradually rises; when the Choir begins to sing the last triplet in the strongest voice and changed melody, the Priest, having again signed three times with the Cross to the east, moves to the south side of the tetrapod and, looking to the north, sings the second petition of the litany and performs an exaltation, similar to the first, also from the east side to the west and from the north to the south, and again, from the west to the east, singing at each petition of the litany, and performs an exaltation similar to the first. And Glory, Both now is sung: "Thou Who Wast lifted up" ("Voznesyisya")[^266].

units.english_text: VENERATION. When the Kontakion of the Cross is sung, the Priest places the Precious Cross on the tetrapod and, at the end of the Kontakion begins to sing "Before Thy Cross" three times. All Who sing bow with their forehead (the sacred minister only with His hand) to the ground after each singing of the troparion. When the Choir sings the stichera of the Cross, the Priest bows once, kisses the Precious Cross and, having bowed again, stands in his place, waiting until other sacred ministers also bow and kiss the Precious Cross[^267]. After this all together with the Priest bow and enter the sanctuary. Other sacred dignitaries, and after them the people, approach and kiss the Precious Cross one by one, bowing before and after this. At the end of the stichera of the Cross the Deacon, if there be one, if – not, then the Priest himself sings two usual litanies: "Have mercy on us, O God" and "Let us complete". Great Dismissal, as usual, with commemoration of the feast[^268].

provenance.verbatim_source: VENERATION. When the Kontakion of the Cross is sung, the Priest places the Precious Cross on the tetrapod and, at the end of the Kontakion begins to sing "Before Thy Cross" three times. All Who sing bow with their forehead (the sacred minister only with His hand) to the ground after each singing of the troparion. When the Choir sings the stichera of the Cross, the Priest bows once, kisses the Precious Cross and, having bowed again, stands in his place, waiting until other sacred ministers also bow and kiss the Precious Cross[^267]. After this all together with the Priest bow and enter the sanctuary. Other sacred dignitaries, and after them the people, approach and kiss the Precious Cross one by one, bowing before and after this. At the end of the stichera of the Cross the Deacon, if there be one, if – not, then the Priest himself sings two usual litanies: "Have mercy on us, O God" and "Let us complete". Great Dismissal, as usual, with commemoration of the feast[^268].

units.english_text: According to our present custom, the Priest, at the end of the Liturgy, vested as he was, in all sacred vestments, having left the chalice on the Holy Table, goes out through the Holy Doors before the tetrapod. While the Choir sings the Troparion "Save, O Lord", the Priest censes the precious Cross from four sides of the tetrapod and, having sung with the Choir and people the Troparion "Before Thy Cross" three times with prostrations, approaches, having bowed, kisses the precious Cross Himself and all others, as many as there be (the Choir sings one of the stichera of the Cross until all kiss). The Choir sings: Glory, Both now: Kontakion to the Cross "Thou Who Wast lifted up". The Priest takes the precious Cross, rests it on his head and carries it through the Holy Doors to the Table of Oblation and returns to the Holy Table, takes the chalice, closes the Holy Doors and withdraws to the sacristy, unvests from the sacred vestments, having said the prayers after Communion, afterwards he dismantles the precious Cross from the basil and puts them away.

units.english_text: The fast of this Forty Days the Lviv Synod limits only to three days of each week, that is Monday, Wednesday and Friday, permitting even on those days dairy, and on other days – to eat meat, but on the condition of the 50th Psalm for the clergy, and 5 "Our Father" and 5 "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos"[^278]  for the faithful, before dinner and before supper. Our custom [is] – to adhere to the fast on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, even if it falls on one of the meat days; we eat nothing with dairy, or very little, until evening. Simple people abstain also from dairy and fast until evening

But today with us and with the Greeks the Lenten service is limited only to Great Lent

units.english_text: The peculiarity of the divine service of this day consists in the fact that on it is taken not only the service of the feast, or on Sunday – also the Resurrectional one, as usually happens on the Apodosis of other feasts, but the service of these two saints is also taken. The reason for this is that the service of these two saints is not transferred to another day, as happens on the Apodosis of other feasts. This can be [the case] when on the Apodosis of other feasts only one service of a saint falls, but here – two, and therefore it is not convenient to transfer it to another day, for then one would have to take three services of saints, and the church rule does not give more than two services. This transfer is all the more inconvenient because these saints have a common troparion and kontakion, although later, in Slavic editions, separate troparia were added to them.

units.english_text: After the proclamation of the dogma of the Immaculate Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos, our hierarchs ordered in their eparchies to celebrate this feast with the same type of divine service as great feasts of the Theotokos are celebrated. And since the old divine service of this feast under the title "Conception of St. Anne" is limited only to one day[^288]  and is not purely of the Theotokos, the Lviv Synod approved the newly composed service of the Immaculate Conception of the Most Holy Theotokos and ordered it to be sung in all our churches for 9 days, of which the first, that is 8 December, comprises the Forefeast, the second – the Feast, the following six – the Afterfeast, and the last (16 December) – the Apodosis of the feast. And in order not to discard the old service (9 December), it ordered to transfer it back to 8 December, as the service of the Forefeast, however, giving it a small type, that is, ordinary.

units.english_text: The Forefeast, Feast, Afterfeast and Apodosis of this feast are celebrated exactly according to the general rule of great feasts of the Theotokos, as is prescribed in the newly published *Anthologion*. However, if its Afterfeast or Apodosis falls on the Sunday of the Forefathers (the second before the Nativity of Christ), which begins on 11 December, then according to the rule approved by the Synod, the divine service is celebrated according to the rule of the Sunday of the Holy Fathers of the First Nicene Council, which is before the Descent of the Holy Spirit, since in both these cases three homogeneous services are taken: Resurrectional, Afterfeast (here – of the Immaculate Conception, there – of the Ascension) and of the Fathers. We will give the rule for this case below, in the rule for the Sunday of the Forefathers.

units.english_text: The Gospel of this Sunday is the same as that of the Sunday of the Forefathers, that is, about the man Who prepared a great supper. If the 28th Sunday falls on the Sunday of the Forefathers, then at the Liturgy only one, the above-mentioned, Gospel is read; but Apostles – two: of the Forefathers, and also of the 28th Sunday. If the 28th Sunday falls directly before or after the Sunday of the Forefathers, read one Gospel about the man Who prepared a great supper, and "on the 28th Sunday read the sequential one which falls on another Sunday"[^289]. If the 28th Sunday falls directly before the Sunday of the Forefathers, then on the Sunday of the Forefathers the 29th sequential Sunday falls, and it is transferred back, to the 28th Sunday. If the 28th Sunday falls directly after the Sunday of the Forefathers, then on the Sunday of the Forefathers the 27th sequential Sunday falls and it is transferred forward, to the 28th Sunday. Similar will be with the Apostle of the 29th sequential Sunday, which will be the same as that of the Sunday of the Forefathers, that is "Brethren, when Christ appears", although the typikon says nothing about this.

units.english_text: The Gospels of these Sundays are usually combined with the Gospels of the *Menaion* Sundays that relate to the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, however, not always identically, but more or less, depending on the greater or lesser distance of the Sunday of the Publican from Theophany. This distance will be greater when Pascha falls later and smaller when Pascha falls earlier. For Pascha can fall on one of 35 days: from 22 March to 25 April, both inclusive. The greater distance between Theophany and the Sunday of the Publican, that is the *Triodion*, will be when Pascha falls on 25 April, for in this case the Sunday of the Publican, the tenth before the Resurrection, falls on 14 February and the distance between Theophany and the *Triodion* will be 38 days, that is 5 weeks and three days, for, having subtracted 6 days from January, 25 will remain, to them are added 13 days of February, and it will be 38; and dividing by 7, it will be 5 integers and 3 remainder. The smaller distance will be when Pascha falls on 22 March, for then the Sunday of the Publican falls on 11 January, and the distance between Theophany and the *Triodion*, that is between 6 and 11 January, will be only 4 days, in the number of which there will not be a single Sunday, for the 4 days before the Sunday of the Publican will be weekdays, namely Saturday, Friday, Thursday and Wednesday.

units.english_text: If the last sequential Sundays are transferred to the Sundays that are lacking between the Sunday after the Enlightenment and the *Triodion*, then according to the rule of our Sluzhebnik[^292], with the Sunday Gospels the weekday Gospels are also transferred. Therefore, even on the weekdays which belong to the cycle of *Menaion* Sundays that relate to the Nativity of Christ and to Theophany, the above-mentioned Gospels of the weekday days should be discarded and the Apostle-Gospel of the services of the saints of the menologion or of various services for every need should be read. If someone wants to repeat the past ones, He can repeat any past week, at His own desire, as the Evangelistarion prescribes: Αναποδιζειν δει όπισθεν, και αναγινωσκειν όθεν ύελεις.

units.english_text: Answer: We learn about this with the help of the boundary key, which is at the end of the *Horologion* and this typikon, and is given for every year. Having seen which of the 35 boundary keys and which of the 35 Paschal days corresponding to them falls then, we calculate all the days that are between Theophany and the nearest Pascha, and having subtracted from them 10 weeks, that is 70 days, which will be from Pascha back to the Publican, we divide the remainder by 7, and the quotient will give the number of Sundays. If the remainder is not divisible by 7, then there will not be a single one. We give two examples: one, if Pascha falls earlier, and the second – if later.

units.english_text: Regarding the superfluous ones, we think that this will never take place. Regarding the lack, we consider that Apostle-Gospels can be lacking at most for five Sundays. To understand this, one must know that Pascha, which follows directly, can fall one or two weeks earlier, or two or three weeks later, than the past one. This conclusion can be made if one compares all the boundary keys of a whole indiction, year after year. Thus, the latest Pascha can fall five weeks later than the previous one, however, with intervals, and not directly from year to year. In that case, if from Pascha to Pascha a whole year ran sequentially, that is 52 weeks, then Apostle-Gospels would be lacking for two Sundays, for they exist only for 50, namely: 18 of the *Triodion* and 32 outside the *Triodion*. If, therefore, the following Pascha falls two weeks earlier than the past one, then from Pascha to Pascha only 50 weeks pass and, thus, the number of Apostle-Gospels equals the number of weeks that pass from Pascha to Pascha, for of those too – 50, thus, there will be no superfluous ones. If from Pascha to Pascha 51 weeks pass, then Apostle-Gospels will be lacking for one week, if 53 (52, namely exactly one year, cannot be), then they will be lacking for 3 weeks; if 54, then they will be lacking for four weeks; if 55, then they will be lacking for five weeks. This lack of sequential Sundays can be filled by the *Menaion* Sundays which belong to the cycle of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, however, not by all five, but only by four, for the Sunday of the Forefathers and the 28th sequential have the same Gospel, and therefore merge into one Sunday. Therefore one of the past sequential Sundays must be repeated after the Sunday after the Enlightenment.

units.english_text: > **Note:** This Sunday, the second before the Nativity of Christ, can fall during the course of seven days, from 11 to 17 December inclusive. Therefore it can fall either in the middle of the feast of the Conception, which is given up on 16 December, or outside, namely 17 December. And since the one that is in the middle of the feast can fall with a Saint either without Polyeleos, which usually happens, or with Polyeleos, as on 13 December, when the Service of St. Eustratius, according to our and Russian typikons, is taken with Polyeleos[^295], the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers has three cases: 1. In the middle of the feast (of the Immaculate Conception) with a Saint without Polyeleos; 2. In the middle of the feast with a Saint with Polyeleos; 3. Outside the feast, that is 17 December. Thus, the Sunday of the Forefathers limits the service of a Saint without Polyeleos to Compline, with the exception of the service of 17 December, that is of the Holy Prophet Daniel and the three youths. Although this service is without Polyeleos, nevertheless, because it has a special relationship to the service of the Forefathers, it is combined with the service of the Forefathers. Now we will give the rule for the three above-mentioned cases.

units.english_text: This Sunday can fall on one of seven days, starting from 18 to 24 December. But since 20 December the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ begins, this Sunday can fall either outside, or in the middle of the Forefeast. Furthermore, if this Sunday falls on the last day of the Forefeast, that is 24 December, on the very Eve of the Nativity of Christ, then it has a separate rule. Therefore this Sunday has three separate rules: one for outside the Forefeast, that is on 18 and 19 December; the second for in the middle of the Forefeast, with the exception of the Eve, that is 20, 21, 22 or 23 December; the third for the Eve, that is for 24 December, as we present.

But since 20 December the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ begins, this Sunday can fall either outside, or in the middle of the Forefeast. Therefore this Sunday has three separate rules: one for outside the Forefeast, that is on 18 and 19 December; the second for in the middle of the Forefeast, with the exception of the Eve, that is 20, 21, 22 or 23 December; the third for the Eve, that is for 24 December, as we present.

units.english_text: From 20 December to 14 January, that is until the Apodosis of Theophany, the *Octoechos* canon to the Theotokos is not taken; in the Forefeast of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany the canon of the Forefeast is taken: sometimes one three-ode canon (22, 23 December), sometimes one three-ode canon and a second two-ode canon with it (20 December, 2 January); sometimes two three-ode canons (3 January), sometimes an eight-ode canon (22, 24 December, 4, 5 January). These canons are taken thus: if there is only one canon, then the Heirmoi of each of its odes are taken twice each, troparia on 6 and, again the same Heirmos once for conclusion (instead of Katavasia); if there are two canons, then only the Heirmoi of the first canon are taken twice each, and the Heirmoi of the second canon are taken only once, and this only at the end of each ode; troparia of both canons together on 6. The refrain to the troparia of the canon will be: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "Glory" – on the penultimate, "Both now" – on the last, only instead of "Glory" at the 8th ode, we sing: "Let us bless the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Lord"[^304]; and to the Katavasia we sing: "We praise, we bless" and the rest, as at Matins. The Katavasia is sung by both choirs together with a bow at its end, at the 8th and 9th odes; also after the Heirmos of the 9th ode, before the troparia, a bow is prescribed[^305]. Otherwise at the 3rd, 6th and 9th odes the canon has nothing. After the canon – either *“It is truly meet”*, as the Moscow Typikon gives on 20 December, or only the Heirmos of the 9th ode, as the Pochaiv and Lviv Trefologia give on 2 January.

units.english_text: Nothing special, except the Liturgy of Basil the Great with Vespers of the Feast on the Eve of the Nativity and Theophany, if they fall on one of the five fast days, from Monday to Friday. For if they fall on Saturday or on Sunday, then on the Eve there will be the Liturgy of Chrysostom, at its proper time without Vespers, and afterwards – Vespers of the Feast, at its proper time. On the Feast itself – Liturgy of Basil the Great without Vespers. On Friday, before the Eve, to which the Royal Hours are transferred, the typikon gives no Liturgy, this is adhered to also by the Lviv Synod[^307].

units.english_text: When, after the Troparion of the Forefeast "Once Mary was registered", the Theotokion is also read, the choirs sing three stichera idiomesa[^314]  on 6, that is twice each. The first stichera both the first and the second time is sung without a refrain; the second – the first time with a separate refrain, and the second – with another separate refrain; the third – the first time with the refrain "Glory", and the second – with the refrain "Both now". All four above-mentioned refrains at all Hours – are the same. At the 9th Hour the third stichera is taken three times, that is the first time it is read loudly and piously by the canonarch in the middle of the church, without a refrain, then the second time – by one choir with the refrain "Glory", and the third – by the other with the refrain "Both now"[^315].

units.english_text: After the singing of the three stichera there will be three readings: the first – of the Prophecy with a Prokimenon, the second – of the Apostle without a Prokimenon and without Alleluia, the third – of the Gospel, beginning it from "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear". All this is accompanied by the following actions: when the stichera end, the Priest puts on a phelonion and, having gone out before the steps of the altar and having bowed, opens the Holy Doors and exclaims: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!" (blessing the people), "Wisdom! Let us attend!". The choirs sing the Prokimenon. After its conclusion the Priest, having exclaimed before the title of the Prophecy "Wisdom!" and before the reading "Let us attend!", waits before the steps of the altar for the end of the reading of the Prophecy and, after its conclusion, having exclaimed "Wisdom!" and "Let us attend!" before the reading of the Apostle, as usual, puts incense into the censer with the short prayer "Incense we offer to Thee" and, having blessed the incense with the words "Blessed is our God", censes everything as usual, that is the Holy Table from four sides, the iconostasis, the choirs and the people[^316]. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, the candle-bearers go out before the analogion, and the Priest approaches the Holy Table and, having bowed, takes the Holy Gospel and, having placed it on the analogion, begins to sing the Gospel from "Wisdom, attend". After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the reading, leaves it there, closes the Holy Doors and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, goes out to the sacristy, takes off the phelonion, goes out through the side doors before the Holy Doors for "Thou Who at all times" and remains there until the end of the Hour.

provenance.verbatim_source: After the singing of the three stichera there will be three readings: the first – of the Prophecy with a Prokimenon, the second – of the Apostle without a Prokimenon and without Alleluia, the third – of the Gospel, beginning it from "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear". All this is accompanied by the following actions: when the stichera end, the Priest puts on a phelonion and, having gone out before the steps of the altar and having bowed, opens the Holy Doors and exclaims: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!" (blessing the people), "Wisdom! Let us attend!". The choirs sing the Prokimenon. After its conclusion the Priest, having exclaimed before the title of the Prophecy "Wisdom!" and before the reading "Let us attend!", waits before the steps of the altar for the end of the reading of the Prophecy and, after its conclusion, having exclaimed "Wisdom!" and "Let us attend!" before the reading of the Apostle, as usual, puts incense into the censer with the short prayer "Incense we offer to Thee" and, having blessed the incense with the words "Blessed is our God", censes everything as usual, that is the Holy Table from four sides, the iconostasis, the choirs and the people[^316]. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, both deacons stand with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all three together to the Holy Mysteries, go out from the sanctuary: the Priest with the Gospel through the middle [doors], and the deacons, having swapped their sides, through the side doors to the analogion. Having bowed low, the deacons return through their doors to the sanctuary and, together with the Priest, close the Holy Doors. Having bowed low all three together to the Holy Mysteries, they withdraw: the deacons to their places, and the Priest before the iconostasis for "Thou Who at all times".

units.english_text: After the concluding prayer of the 9th Hour we immediately read the Typika just as in the *Horologion*, however, without the introductory verse that is before the first psalm, without the stichera on the "Beatitudes", without the Apostle-Gospel; also, if there be Liturgy, then also without the "Creed" and without "Blessed be the name of the Lord", and without the following 33rd Psalm, for all this will be taken at the Liturgy. When the Royal Hours are transferred back, to Friday, then since then there will be no Liturgy, here both the "Creed" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" with the 33rd Psalm is read. Instead of the kontakia of the temple, of the day and others, one Kontakion of the Eve is taken. Here is the detailed rule for you.

coordinates.section: 3.4.8.8 In the arch-cathedral church Vespers with the Service of Basil begins at 10.30. If the Eve falls on Saturday or on Sunday, then the Service of Chrysostom without Vespers will be at 08.30, and Vespers separately begins at 11.00, in order to hasten the Holy Supper, which according to the typikon should begin later, that is at 3 o'clock in the afternoon (current 1 o'clock after noon) on the Eve of the Nativity, and on the ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany – in the evening hours, that is at the usual time. All-Night Vigil with Compline – at the usual time. Now we will give three detailed rules: one – for the case of Vespers with the Service of Basil, one – for the case of Vespers which is celebrated separately, without the Service, and one – for the All-Night Vigil with Great Compline

After the singing before the steps of the altar "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!", "Wisdom, let us attend!" the Priest withdraws behind the Holy Table and sits there during the readings in his place. units.english_text: 1. The Priest, having put on an epitrachelion and having gone out before the Holy Doors, bows low and begins the usual: "Blessed is our God". Choirs: "Amen", also "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and the rest with the Trisagion and "Our Father" up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive[^320]. units.english_text: 9. After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the Gospel reading and having given [it] to the first deacon to kiss, also to the second, approaches the Holy Table, on which he places the Holy Gospel, which remains there. The deacons, having bowed low before the steps of the Holy Table, go out, each through HIS doors, before the Holy Doors and, having bowed low, first the second Deacon exclaims "Let us all say", and also the first after "Vouchsafe" – the litany "Let us complete". If there be no deacons, then the Priest himself sings the litanies from the Holy Table and immediately after the second exclamation of the litany "Let us complete" gives the Great Dismissal of the Feast itself. (On Theophany there is no dismissal here, but it will be after the Blessing of Water)

units.english_text: After the end of the second tripalm the choirs sing alternatingly "God is with us", that is selected verses of the eighth ode of the prophecies of Isaiah. They sing thus: 1st choir: "God is with us, understand ye nations,... for God is with us", afterwards the second choir sings the same. Also other verses the choirs sing alternatingly, ending each verse with the words "For God is with us". After the end of all verses they sing "God is with us" three times[^327]. The custom of singing the whole first verse after each of the following ones as is usually done here, we do not find in any typikon[^328]. The Lviv Synod also adds that the Priest should not go out before the Holy Doors and sing these verses alternatingly with the choirs, but only there/, where there will be only one choir, for then the Priest replaces one of the choirs. Similarly he should not go out for the moleben verses "O Most Holy Lady", which the choirs say twice, that is once one, and once the other choir, but only, if there be one choir[^329]

units.english_text: > **Note:** This Saturday has three cases: it can fall either on the first, or on the last day of the Afterfeast of the Nativity of Christ, or on others. When it falls on the first day, that is 26 December, then it is taken with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos and has a separate rule; when – on the last, that is 31 December, then it is taken with the Apodosis of the feast of the Nativity and has a separate rule; if on others, that is 27, 28, 29 and 30 December, then it also has a separate rule. We will give consistently all three rules.

units.english_text: Now, if you wish to know how many Saturdays and Sundays there will be in a given year between the Nativity and Theophany, then first of all you must find out on which day of the week the Nativity of Christ falls, afterwards, going along the transverse line from that day of the week to Theophany, you will find the number of Saturdays and Sundays between the Nativity and Theophany. Regarding the rule which will be for these Saturdays and Sundays in the case when there will be two Saturdays and two Sundays (as in the 4th, 5th and 6th rows), there will be no inconsistency, as there will be no inconsistency in the case when either two Saturdays, or two Sundays (as in the 3rd and 7th rows), for these two Saturdays and two Sundays have their unchangeable rule. But all inconsistencies are limited to the case of only one Saturday or Sunday (as in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 7th rows). In this case two questions arise:

units.english_text: To the first question we answer: if this Saturday or Sunday is in the middle of the feast of the Nativity, that is within December, then the Saturday or Sunday after the Nativity is taken; if – outside the feast of the Nativity, that is within January, then the Saturday or Sunday before Theophany is taken. Regarding the second question, that is what to do with one Saturday or Sunday which sometimes has no place, we answer: Greek books give no rule for this and therefore this Saturday or Sunday should not have been taken. However, the Slavs do not wish to discard anything and give the following rules for this case.

units.english_text: The Saturday, which will be the one between the Nativity and Theophany can fall either in the middle, or outside the feast of the Nativity: in the middle, namely 30 or 31 December so, as in the first and second rows; outside the feast, namely 1 January, as in the 7th row. If, therefore, it falls in the middle of the feast, then the Apostle-Gospel will be first of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity, and after – of the Saturday before Theophany. Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn on 30 December will be only of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity; on 31 December, that is on the Apodosis of the feast – will be only of the Feast. If, therefore, it falls outside the feast, as in the 6th row, that is 1 January, then the Apostle-Gospel will be first to the Circumcision, for the Saturday does not have them. On ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity the Apostle-Gospel is taken on the Apodosis of the feast, 31 December. Prokimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn – only of the Feast.

units.english_text: If there be one Sunday between the Nativity and Theophany, then, similarly as for Saturday, it falls either in the middle of the feast, that is 30 or 31 December, as in the 3rd and 2nd rows, or outside the feast, that is 1 January with the Circumcision, as in the 1st row. And if it falls in the middle of the feast, then the Sunday after the Nativity is taken on 30 or 31 December according to the rule given here on p. 182-183. And the Sunday before Theophany is taken on 1 January in the first place, also the Circumcision and everything else according to the rule which is given for 1 January, when it falls on a Sunday. If the Sunday is one and falls on 1 January, as in the 1st row, then the Sunday after the Nativity is taken on 26 December with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos according to the rule given here on p. 181[^337].

One peculiarity of this day – at Matins, for St. Protomartyr (according to others also the Feast) has both Stichera of the Praises, and afterwards – Small Doxology, and Aposticha in its place. Finally our people even on this day abstain from work and take part in the divine service.

units.english_text: In general typikons the divine service of this day is not given with All-Night Vigil, but only with Polyeleos. However, probably for the sake of the beginning of the civil year, or also for Basil the Great, for many years All-Night Vigil has been served with us, because it is already given in the Pochaiv *Anthologion* of 1777[^339]. We will present the rule first for weekdays, and then for Sunday.

provenance.verbatim_source: In general typikons the divine service of this day is not given with All-Night Vigil, but only with Polyeleos. However, probably for the sake of the beginning of the civil year, or also for Basil the Great, for many years All-Night Vigil has been served with us, because it is already given in the Pochaiv *Anthologion* of 1777[^339]. We will present the rule first for weekdays, and then for Sunday.

If the Nativity of Christ, and consequently 1 January, falls on Monday or Tuesday, then the Sunday before Theophany will not take place, as the table on p. 184 shows, and then later Slavic typikons[^343]  give the Prokimenon, Apostle-Gospel and Communion Hymn of that Sunday on 1 January with the Circumcision, thus, according to such a rule, which should have been given on 1 January on a Sunday, the Sunday before Theophany takes the first place, after it – the Circumcision; the Apostle-Gospel of Basil falls out

units.english_text: After the Prayer behind the Ambo, if Saturday or Sunday, then after the dismissal of Vespers, the church cross-bearer stands between two candle-bearers in the middle of the church, and before Him – a church server with three candlesticks, with a censer and with a vessel for incense. The Deacon takes the Holy Gospel from the table, the Priest takes the cross with his right hand and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, they go out through the Holy Doors: first the Deacon with the Gospel, behind him – the Priest with the cross, vested in all sacred vestments of his rank, and the Choir sings the Troparion "The voice of the Lord"[^347]; all proceed to the narthex of the church. When all have gone out there, the Deacon places the Holy Gospel, and the Priest – the cross on a table covered with a tablecloth or a clean cloth, on which there will be also a wide vessel with water; and immediately the Priest censes the table from four sides and all present, according to the order.

When all have gone out there, the Deacon places the Holy Gospel, and the Priest – the cross on a table covered with a tablecloth or a clean cloth, on which there will be also a wide vessel with water; and immediately the Priest censes the table from four sides and all present, according to the order.

Then the Priest reads the Gospel, before which the first Deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, attend" and the rest, and the second: "Let us attend".

units.english_text: After the singing of the Gospel the Deacon says the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", during which the Priest reads quietly the prayer "O Lord Jesus Christ"; and after the prayer He does not exclaim, but says to Himself: "Amen". And when "For the precipitous, pure" is said, the Priest begins loudly this prayer: "Great Art Thou, O Lord"[^348]. The prayer "O Trinity beyond all being", since it is given only in some editions, may be omitted; this is allowed by the *Euchologion* of Benedict, although our typikons do not allow this[^349].

units.english_text: In the prayer "Great Art Thou, O Lord" three members are exclaimed three times, namely the first member "Great Art Thou, O Lord", at which the Priest three times crosswise signs the water with three lit candles[^350]; the second "Thou Thyself, therefore", at which He blesses the water with His hand, immersing His fingers crosswise; the third "Thou Thyself and now", at which He breathes three times crosswise on the water. When He exclaims: "And save, O Lord, Thy servants, the Most Holy Ecumenical Primate (Name) the Pope of Rome[^351]  and our faithful Emperor (Name)" the Choir sings "Many Years".

units.english_text: At the end of this prayer the Choir: "Amen"; priest: "Peace be unto all" and, after the prayer at the bowing of heads, which he says quietly, he exclaims: "For Thou Art the sanctification" and immediately blesses with the cross: immerses it simply into the water, holding with both hands, and sings this troparion: "When in Jordan"[^352], and all the people sing with Him. "And the second time singing the same troparion"[^353], and all the people sing with Him. Then the server pours holy water onto a tray or into a sprinkler. The Priest turns his face to the west, holding the precious cross with his left hand, and with the right – the sprinkler, and sprinkles all the people with holy water. After this the choirs sing Glory, Both now: Stichera "Let us praise, O faithful", the procession returns to the church in the same way, and the Priest sprinkles on all sides[^354], and thus they enter the sanctuary through the Holy Doors: the Deacon with the Gospel, and after him the Priest with the cross. And when the Priest has sprinkled the entire sanctuary, the Deacon places the Gospel, and the Priest the cross on the Holy Table, in its place, and the Choir sings "Blessed be the name of the Lord", if there be Vespers with the Service of Basil; if Vespers – separate from the Holy Liturgy, then immediately the Great Dismissal of the Feast; at the end: Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast, which both choirs sing together in the middle of the church, as at Vespers with the Service of Basil on 25 December.

units.english_text: This Synaxis can fall either on weekdays, or on a Sunday. Its service has the appearance of a Saint on 6 without Polyeleos, but with the Great Doxology. Vespers will be with an Entrance, in view of the Great Prokimenon of the Feast. Matins from the beginning to the canon – of small type, from the canon to the end – of great type. Here is the rule for both cases.

units.english_text: In January fall five saints, whose memory we honor with Polyeleos without All-Night Vigil, that is 11 January – Ven. Theodosius, 17 January – Anthony the Great, 20 January – Euthymius the Great, 25 January – Gregory the Theologian, 27 January – Translation of the relics of Chrysostom, and since the *Triodion* can begin within the limits of 35 days, from 11 January to 14 February, therefore these saints can fall either outside, or in the middle of the *Triodion*: in the middle of the *Triodion*, if the beginning of the *Triodion* falls on one of the days from 11 to 27 January; outside the *Triodion*, if the beginning of the *Triodion* falls on one of the days from 28 January to 14 February. And if they fall outside the *Triodion*, then their services are subject to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos; if they fall in the middle of the *Triodion*, they should have a separate rule, and since church books do not give it, we will give it.

provenance.verbatim_source: In January fall five saints, whose memory we honor with Polyeleos without All-Night Vigil, that is 11 January – Ven. Theodosius, 17 January – Anthony the Great, 20 January – Euthymius the Great, 25 January – Gregory the Theologian, 27 January – Translation of the relics of Chrysostom, and since the *Triodion* can begin within the limits of 35 days, from 11 January to 14 February, therefore these saints can fall either outside, or in the middle of the *Triodion*: in the middle of the *Triodion*, if the beginning of the *Triodion* falls on one of the days from 11 to 27 January; outside the *Triodion*, if the beginning of the *Triodion* falls on one of the days from 28 January to 14 February. And if they fall outside the *Triodion*, then their services are subject to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos; if they fall in the middle of the *Triodion*, they should have a separate rule, and since church books do not give it, we will give it.

units.english_text: St. Gregory and Chrysostom can fall not only with the Sunday of the Publican and of the Prodigal [Son], but also with the Meatfare, for when the *Triodion* begins on 18 or 20 January, then the Sunday of the Prodigal [Son] will be 25 or 27 January, and when the *Triodion* begins on 11 or 13 January, then 25 or 27 January will be Meatfare Sunday. These saints can fall also on the Saturday of Souls, that is Meatfare, which precedes Meatfare Sunday. If the *Triodion* begins on 12 or 14 January, then 25 or 27 falls on Meatfare Saturday. Chrysostom can fall also on Cheesefare Tuesday, which will be after Meatfare Sunday, for if 25 January falls on Meatfare Sunday, then 27 January will be Cheesefare Tuesday.

units.english_text: If one of these saints falls outside the *Triodion*, one should adhere to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos. If he falls in the middle of the *Triodion*, as e. g. St. Theodosius can fall on the Sunday of the Publican, he must be transferred to another day. If one of the four other saints falls on the Sunday of the Publican, of the Prodigal [Son], Meatfare, on Meatfare Saturday or on Cheesefare Tuesday, then one must adhere to the rule of the Three Hierarchs, given in the *Menaion* on 30 January, which we will give immediately, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, which will not be here, but there will be it at Great Vespers, at the end. Resurrectional Troparion, Glory: of the Saint, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint. At Compline, after *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the *Triodion*[^361].

units.english_text: Our and Russian church rules do not give for this case All-Night Vigil, and consequently neither Small Vespers, but only one Great, without blessing of loaves; afterwards also Compline, at which after *“It is truly meet”* – Kontakion of the Saints. All this according to the rule of the Forerunner on 24 February[^365]. However, since with us even in this case All-Night Vigil is served, although there is no rule for it, we will give the rule of the All-Night Vigil also for this case, similarly to the rule of the Meeting on 2 February, if it falls on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday of Cheesefare week.

units.english_text: If the Three Hierarchs fall on one of the days of Cheesefare week, then the three-ode canon of Matins we sing at Compline, namely: if the Feast is on Monday, then at Compline on Sunday; if on Tuesday, then on Wednesday; if on Wednesday, then on Thursday; if on Thursday, then on Tuesday; if on Friday, then on Wednesday. Thus give our and Russian typikons for the Feast of the Meeting on these days. Only, if the Feast falls on Monday, let the three-ode canon be sung on Tuesday, for when there is All-Night Vigil – Compline does not happen.

units.english_text: This feast falls on 2 February and therefore can fall either in the middle, or outside the *Triodion*. And since the first boundary of the *Triodion* is 11 January, and the last – 14 February, therefore it can fall at most 22 days from the beginning of the *Triodion* and 12 days before the beginning of the *Triodion*. When there is the earliest boundary of the *Triodion*, that is 11 January, then the feast reaches Monday of the first week of Lent, the next – immediately after the fourth Sunday of the *Triodion*, that is after Cheesefare Sunday. And if it falls outside the *Triodion*, then its order is celebrated according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos, although partly it is of the Lord. It differs from a feast of the Theotokos only by a separate dismissal and at the Liturgy – by a separate entrance verse, and on the Apodosis there will not be the Apostle-Gospel of the Feast and of the day, as for the Theotokos, but only of the day, as for the Lord. And if it falls on a Sunday, its service is combined with the Resurrectional, according to the rule of a feast of the Theotokos. It has one day of Forefeast and seven days of Afterfeast, for it is given up on 9 February.

euchological_and_rubrical_metadata.structural_slot: 3.6 February :: II. FOREFEAST OF THE MEETING ON MEATFARE SATURDAY

units.english_text: When the Forefeast of the Meeting falls on Meatfare Saturday, then the service of the Forefeast we sing on the previous Friday with Saints Cyrus, John and Tryphon[^367], according to the general rule of two saints on 4 in the Forefeast, only at *“Lord, I have cried”* there will be stichera: of the Forefeast – 3 and to the Holy Unmercenaries – 3, and the stichera of Tryphon are taken in the morning at the Praises on 4; Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast[^368]. After them, at the Aposticha, – stichera of the Forefeast with their refrains. On Meatfare Saturday we sing the general order for the deceased.

After them, at the Aposticha, – stichera of the Forefeast with their refrains. On Meatfare Saturday we sing the general order for the deceased.

euchological_and_rubrical_metadata.structural_slot: 3.6 February :: III. FOREFEAST OF THE MEETING

units.english_text: Everything according to the general rule of a Saint on 4 in the Forefeast, only at the Aposticha of Vespers, and also at Matins, there will not be stichera of the Forefeast, but idiomesa of the *Triodion* of the day twice and to the Martyr with general refrains; also Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast. And at Matins, after the 2nd Kathisma there will not be the Sessional hymn of the Forefeast, but of the *Triodion*. The canon, where the three-ode canon comes, will be of the Forefeast with Heirmos on 4, three troparia of the Saint on 2 and of the *Triodion* on 8[^369]; katavasia at the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th – Heirmos of the canon of the Saint. Generally, in those odes where the three-ode canon comes, there will be the Katavasia of the *Triodion*.

And at Matins, after the 2nd Kathisma there will not be the Sessional hymn of the Forefeast, but of the *Triodion*. The canon, where the three-ode canon comes, will be of the Forefeast with Heirmos on 4, three troparia of the Saint on 2 and of the *Triodion* on 8[^369]; katavasia at the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th – Heirmos of the canon of the Saint. Generally, in those odes where the three-ode canon comes, there will be the Katavasia of the *Triodion*.

units.english_text: This Apodosis can fall either in the middle, or outside the *Triodion*. In the middle of the *Triodion*, if the *Triodion* falls on one of 30 days from 11 January to 9 February inclusive; outside the *Triodion*, if it falls on other five days, from 10 to 14 February. And if it falls outside the *Triodion*, then the Apodosis will be 9 February, according to the general rule of the Apodosis of a feast of the Theotokos; And in this case the Afterfeast has 7 days inclusive with the Apodosis. But if it falls in the middle of the *Triodion*, then the number of days of the Afterfeast from 7 can be reduced to 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, and the reason for this – various services of the *Triodion*, with which it coincides. However, this reduction does not always take place in the middle of the *Triodion*, but only when the Apodosis of the Feast coincides with certain services of the *Triodion*, which are incompatible with the service of the Feast. Such are: Meatfare Saturday (of Souls), Meatfare Sunday, which is of the Last Judgment, Cheesefare Wednesday and Friday, which have a completely Lenten rule, and Monday of the 1st week of Lent, on which the day of 9 February can fall, and partially also Cheesefare Sunday. Generally one can establish such a rule: if Pascha falls on days from 8 April and earlier, and the *Triodion* – from 28 January and earlier, then the Apodosis of the Meeting will be 9 February, that is on the seventh day after the Feast. When in a given year the Apodosis of the Feast will be at its proper time, and earlier, when there will be no Apodosis at all, the following table, compiled according to the rules of Slavic menaia, will show.

coordinates.section: 3.6.4.1 Since the last boundary of the Triodion is 14 February, this feast always falls in the middle of the Triodion. If the Triodion is earlier, then this feast enters all the deeper into the Triodion and coincides with many Triodion services. Even more, this feast can coincide with other services, given in the Triodion from Wednesday of Meatfare Week to Tuesday of the 8th week of the Triodion, that is of the 4th of Great Lent, inclusive. The last boundary of the beginning of the Triodion is 14 February, and after subtracting from 14 February 13 days, which precede the beginning of the Triodion, 11 will remain, dividing which by 7, we will get in the quotient 1, with 4 in the remainder, that is one whole week and one not whole – the first four days; and since the first day of the first week is Sunday (for the Triodion begins on Sunday), then the first day of the second week will be Sunday, the second – Monday, the third – Tuesday, the fourth – Wednesday. And since the first Sunday of the Triodion is the Sunday of the Publican, the second – of the Prodigal [Son], the third – Meatfare, then the Wednesday on which the Finding falls will be Meatfare Wednesday (for in the Lenten Triodion the days of the week are named after the following Sunday), as the earliest boundary of this feast in relation to the Triodion. And that the last boundary of this feast in relation to the Triodion is Tuesday of the 4th week of Great Lent is proven thus. The first boundary of the Triodion is 11 January, from which to 24 February will be 45 days, dividing which by 7, we will get 6 whole weeks with a remainder of 3; but, since the first day of this remainder is Sunday, as is the first day of each of the 6 past weeks, it will be the 7th Sunday of the Triodion, and the second day will be Monday, the third – Tuesday of the 8th week of the Triodion, of the 4th of Great Lent

units.english_text: On other days – Great Compline. We do not take the Trisagion. Small Dismissal, as at Small Compline

units.english_text: > **Note:** On the Forefeast the typikon prescribes the Service of the Presanctified, as also on Saints with Polyeleos; however, with us the Service of the Presanctified is sung only on Wednesday and Friday, and on other days – of Chrysostom. When the Service of the Presanctified was supposed to be according to the typikon, but is not celebrated, then 3 stichera, which are at the Aposticha, should be transferred to *“Lord, I have cried”*, and after them sing both 3 prosomia stichera of the *Triodion*, and 3 of the Forefeast. On Wednesday evening the stichera from the Aposticha do not need to be transferred to *“Lord, I have cried”*, for they are already given in the *Triodion* at *“Lord, I have cried”*.

units.english_text: > **Note:** If the feast falls on Monday, then on Sunday evening it has two Vespers: one Small, and the second – Great with Matins, with which it comprises the All-Night Vigil; if the feast falls on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, then on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evening it has only one Great Vespers together with the Liturgy of the Presanctified, and afterwards – Great Compline with Matins, with which it comprises the All-Night Vigil. And since today with us the Liturgy of the Presanctified is celebrated only on Wednesdays and Fridays of Great Lent, we give for Vespers of this feast three rules: one – for Sunday evening, the second – for Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, the third – for Wednesday evening.

And since today with us the Liturgy of the Presanctified is celebrated only on Wednesdays and Fridays of Great Lent, we give for Vespers of this feast three rules: one – for Sunday evening, the second – for Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, the third – for Wednesday evening.

units.english_text: > **Note:** Our handwritten typikon, *Tserkovne Oko* and others transfer the service of the Akathist to another time, for example to the 4th Saturday of Lent, or to the Sunday of the 5th week. The new Constantinopolitan Typikon transfers it to Thursday of the 5th week of Lent (of the Great Canon), which it transfers back, to Tuesday. The Pochaiv *Anthologion* and Moscow Typikon combine the service of the Annunciation with the service of the Akathist, and on Matins give a rule similar to the rule of the Annunciation on the Akathist Saturday, only the canon of the Akathist they prescribe on 6 and of the Feast on 8[^409].

provenance.verbatim_source: > **Note:** Our handwritten typikon, *Tserkovne Oko* and others transfer the service of the Akathist to another time, for example to the 4th Saturday of Lent, or to the Sunday of the 5th week. The new Constantinopolitan Typikon transfers it to Thursday of the 5th week of Lent (of the Great Canon), which it transfers back, to Tuesday. The Pochaiv *Anthologion* and Moscow Typikon combine the service of the Annunciation with the service of the Akathist, and on Matins give a rule similar to the rule of the Annunciation on the Akathist Saturday, only the canon of the Akathist they prescribe on 6 and of the Feast on 8[^409].

units.english_text: However, the service of the Annunciation is so great that it does not allow combination with another service, and the service of the Akathist is also great and long, so that it could be sung together with the feast, and therefore, it seems, we have quite serious reasons not to make this combination. Therefore, here too, the Akathist should be transferred to another day, namely, optimally to Monday, Tuesday, or Wednesday of the 5th week, at Compline[^407], and on Thursday we sing the great canon.

units.english_text: Stichera at *“Lord, I have cried”* and at the Aposticha are taken according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos on Sunday. Prokimenon will be great "Who is so great a God as our God". At the Aposticha, after the Doxastikon of the Feast, will be Glory: "It is the Day of Resurrection"; also "Christ is risen" (3), Glory, and now: Troparion of the Feast; "Have mercy on us, O God" and Dismissal.

units.english_text: Everything – according to the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil on Sunday. Only at the end, on the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers, there will be the Troparion to the Saint, Glory, and now: "The noble Joseph". On the Sundays of the Paralytic and of the Samaritan Woman – Resurrectional Troparion, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint.

units.english_text: Can fall with services of the *Triodion* from Friday of Bright Week to Thursday after the Sunday of the Blind Man, the 6th after the Resurrection. It is celebrated according to the rules of St. George, here on p. 280, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, as noted about St. Mark, 25 April. Although St. George does not reach the Sunday of the Blind Man like James, however, the Sunday of the Blind Man has the same rule as the three preceding Sundays, to which St. James reaches. But since on Wednesday after the Sunday of the Blind Man – is the Apodosis of the Resurrection, and on Thursday – Ascension, to which the rules of St. George do not reach, in these two cases one should adhere to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, which we will give below, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, which James does not have.

units.english_text: Can fall with services of the Flowery *Triodion*, from Monday after the Sunday of the Apostle Thomas to the 7th Sunday after the Resurrection (Holy Fathers) inclusive. From Monday after the Sunday of the Apostle Thomas to the Apodosis of the Resurrection adhere to the rule of St. George, here on p. 280. From the Apodosis of the Resurrection and further adhere to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, as we gave on 25 April.

units.english_text: The Service of this day – of small type, without Polyeleos, without Great Doxology and incomplete, for it has only a Troparion and Kontakion, stichera at *“Lord, I have cried”*, a canon at Matins, at the Liturgy – Apostle-Gospel and Communion Hymn to the Cross from 14 September, as our and Russian typikons and the Venetian *Menaion* give, according to others – only Troparion and Kontakion. It coincides with services of the Flowery *Triodion* from Friday before the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers to Thursday before the Descent of the Holy Spirit.

units.english_text: The *Menaion* gives only one rule – for weekdays in the middle of the feast. If, however, this service falls on one of the Sundays of Pentecost, or on some other day, on which the service of a Saint without Polyeleos should be sung at Compline or should be transferred to another day, we think that it too should be subject to this rule. The Service of St. Acacius is sung at Compline.

It is also proper to take their Troparion and Kontakion of the day at the Hours and at the Liturgy if they fall with the Feast of the Eucharist and with the Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos[^440]

units.english_text: In relation to the Feast of the Co-suffering, with which these saints can coincide (for the rule has nothing), they are subject to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, when he falls on the Feast of the Ascension, here on p. 295-296. However, since the Co-suffering does not have All-Night Vigil, at Small Vespers everything is sung only to the Saint, and at Great Matins all sessional hymns will be to the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Feast. Everything else up to the canon – only to the Saints. Canon of the Feast with Heirmos on 6 and to the Saints on 8. If 25 and 30 June, that is the second day of the Feast of these Saints, falls with the Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos, then their service is taken at Compline.

units.english_text: For the case of Sunday church books do not give a rule. We think that at Vespers, if there be no Polyeleos, at *“Lord, I have cried”* there should be 6 Resurrectional stichera and 4 of the Theotokos[^443]. If there be Polyeleos, then 4 Resurrectional and 6 of the Theotokos, Glory: of the Theotokos, Both now: Dogmatikon of the tone. At the Aposticha – Glory, and now: of the Robe. Troparia at the end of Vespers and at *“God is the Lord”* we end with the Troparion of the Robe, and at the Liturgy – with the Kontakion of the Robe.

units.english_text: The Procession of the Precious Cross, which took place once in Constantinople from the imperial palace to the most beautiful church of Sophia, we depict now by the bringing out of the Precious Cross in the evening first from the sacristy to the Holy Table, and then, on the day of 1 August, from the Holy Table to the tetrapod, at Matins during the Doxology, when the Veneration also takes place, according to the rule of 14 September, on p. 120, except the Exaltation, which happens only on 14 September on the Exaltation of the Precious Cross, and here there will be none. Besides this, in Slavic books on this day also the Lesser Blessing of Water is prescribed either at Matins immediately before the Veneration, or later, at another time of the day. In some places also the blessing of herbs takes place, as on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos[^454].

units.english_text: 2. During the singing of the Praises the Priest, having vested in all sacred vestments (of violet color)[^455]  and having exclaimed before the steps of the Holy Table: "Glory to Thee, Who Hast shown us the light", and having censed the precious Cross, carries it out around the Holy Table through the northern doors before the Holy Doors, and after the end of the Great Doxology with the Trisagion, exclaims: "Wisdom, attend", goes before the tetrapod and, having placed the precious Cross on it, when the Choir sings the Troparion "Save, O Lord", censes it from four sides and venerates the precious Cross, everything exactly as on 14 September, here on p. 122-127

units.english_text: Everything – according to the rule of 24 June, however, by the decision of the Lviv Synod, must be transferred from a weekday to Sunday with All-Night Vigil. It is usually transferred to the following Sunday, only if the following Sunday falls on 1 September, then the service is transferred to the previous Sunday, so as not to coincide with three other services, that is Resurrectional, of the Indiction and of St. Simeon[^464]. The fast of the Beheading we do not transfer to Sunday, but keep on the very day of the feast[^465].

units.english_text: The divine services of this week approach the Lenten [order], however, gradually, for Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday have only certain parts in the *Triodion*, while all other parts are filled by the *Octoechos* and *Menaion*. Wednesday and Friday have in the *Triodion* a fuller order of Lenten character with prostrations[^472]. Saturday and Sunday, although they have a full service in the *Triodion*, nevertheless are not of Lenten form, as are all Saturdays and Sundays of Great Lent. The parts that Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday have in the *Triodion* are as follows: 1. Aposticha at Vespers and at Matins. 2. 2nd Sessional Hymn at Matins before the Canon. 3. Canon of the *Triodion*, usually double, that is, with two heirmoi

units.english_text: In view of the Lenten form of the church services of these days, violet vestments should be used, since at Matins, instead of *“God is the Lord”*, "Alleluia" is sung on these days, as on the days of Great Lent; therefore, the Typikon prescribes three prostrations (small) at the beginning of Vespers at the Trisagion and at "O come, let us worship", and also after the pre-introductory psalm at "Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia, glory to Thee, O God"[^477], as well as after each of the three antiphons of the Kathisma (although now we read only the beginning of the Kathisma), after "Vouchsafe, O Lord", and after the Trisagion following "Now letteest Thou Thy servant depart". In addition to this, the Aposticha will be of the *Triodion*.

units.english_text: 4. The prostrations we make at the three first troparia, according to the Typikon – are not great, but small, although due to ignorance of the rubric, or due to excessive piety, great ones are made among us. For here this prostration is called simply metanoia, and with the addition megale [great] it is given only at the prayer of St. Ephrem and never at the end of Vespers, after the litany "Have mercy on us, O God". Likewise at the Great Canon the rubric does not prescribe great prostrations, but simply metanoias

units.english_text: 5. Neither Greek nor Slavonic rubrics give the form of the great or small prostration. However, according to custom it will be thus: he who makes a great prostration falls on his knees and touches the ground with his forehead; he who makes a small prostration does not fall on his knees, nor touches the ground with his forehead, but only crossing himself reaches the ground with his right hand, or only to the knees as the Synod of Lviv prescribes in Title V "On the Holy Liturgy", in the prayers before the iconostasis before the Proskomedia[^481]. We reach the ground with the right hand when we bow to the Holy Mysteries; only to the knees when we bow to holy icons, or at various supplications. However, our people in these parts do not have the custom, when bowing, to extend hands to the ground, or to the knees, but only crossing themselves to bow low before the Holy Mysteries, and higher – in other circumstances. We suppose, however, that at small Lenten prostrations we should reach the knees with the hand, for throughout the whole year at the Trisagion and at "O come, let us worship" we make prostrations, not reaching the knees with the hand[^482]

units.english_text: * *Katavasia:* Katavasia will be the heirmos of the last canon, that is, of the *Triodion*, after each ode, as given in the *Triodion* on Cheesefare Friday, for these two days have a common rubric, although for Wednesday it is given imprecisely. The Canon of the *Octoechos* and *Menaion* in these odes, according to the rubric of the Greek Triodia, is omitted[^492]. The rubrics of the Slavs, for Whom the Greek length is not enough, prescribe transferring the odes of the *Menaion* canon to the preceding ones, in which the triodion has no place, and they sing on Wednesday the 1st ode of the *Octoechos* with heirmos on 4, the 1st and 3rd odes of the *Menaion* (without Theotokia) on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. On Friday – the 4th ode of the *Octoechos* on 4, the 4th and 5th odes of the *Menaion* on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. Similarly, the 6th ode of the *Octoechos* on 4, the 6th and 8th of the *Menaion* on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. Also the 6th ode of the *Octoechos* on 4, the 7th and 9th of the *Menaion* on 6 and the *Triodion* on 4. The Biblical Odes in the Psalter we do not sing[^493]. To the troparia of the canon we chant the usual refrains (on [pp. 29-30](Final_Dolnytsky_part2_general_rubrics.md#refrains-to-the-odes-of-the-canon)).

units.english_text: 3. We sing three Trinity Hymns of the current tone, given in the *Horologion*, three for each tone. They are all sung three times with the refrain "Glory" to the second, and "Both now" – to the third. At each first one we make a commemoration of the weekday service, at the second – a commemoration of all saints, at the third – a commemoration of the Theotokos. However, since the weekday service of the week changes daily, and the troparia are sung the same each day of the week (except Saturdays and Sundays, on which, because they are not Lenten, the Trinity Hymns are not sung), at the end of each first Trinity Hymn a colon is given, which signifies that the troparion must be completed with the commemoration of the weekday service, the form of which is indicated at the end of the 3rd troparion of Tone 1

units.english_text: 6. Odes and Canons. The Biblical Odes, given at the end of the Psalter, are intertwined with the odes of the canon, as given: before the ode of the canon the corresponding ode of the Psalter is recited, leaving its last verses for refrains to the troparia of the canon, in such quantity as there will be troparia in the ode of the canon, including the heirmos, except two, for to the penultimate troparion we refrain "Glory", and to the last – "Both now". The 2nd Ode is recited in full before the ode of the canon, and to the troparia of its canon we refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains to the troparia of the canon. The Greek Typikon prescribes singing the Odes of the Psalter in the tone of the *Menaion* canon, but now we do not even know what their melody was

In some odes there will be 3 canons on 14, that is of the Saint of the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6 and both canons of the *Triodion* on 8: one on 4 and the second on 4. units.english_text: A more precise example of the combination of the Odes of the Psalter with the Odes of the Canon is given at the 1st Ode in the Moscow Typikon, and is presented as follows: "After this we begin: 'Let us sing to the Lord' in the tone of the canon of the *Menaion* of the saint of the day and the verses of the odes are recited hurriedly, each Choir – its verse, until they reach 'The waters became thick' and from this they begin verses on 14, and we sing the *Menaion* with heirmos on 6. And we sing thus: the first Choir reads the verse 'The waters became thick' and sings the heirmos. The second Choir reads the second verse 'The enemy said' and, after it, – the troparion of the canon, and in sequence verses by choirs up to 'Then hastened'. From the verse 'Then hastened' we begin the triodion of Kyr Joseph on 4. And at 'The Lord reigning' we sing the 2nd triodion of Kyr Theodore the Studite, and one choir sings the troparion, and the second choir – the 2nd verse and the troparion. After this both choirs, having united, sing: Glory: Trinity Hymn, in a higher voice, Both now: Theotokion. Then we sing in the highest voice: 'Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee', and we sing the other troparion of Theodore, because the ode has 5 troparia. At the end we sing the Katavasia – heirmos of the second canon"[^515].
