units.english_text: Regarding the refrains to the troparia of the canon, know that in order to find the number of refrains as quickly as possible, the last four, six, and eight verses of the Biblical Odes (except the 2nd, for it is read in full before the heirmos) from the bottom up are marked in the middle of the song, or on the side, with the inscription: "on 4, on 6, on 8". But on 14 they are not counted off, since 6 verses from 8 upwards are easily counted. However, the counting of 14 verses in current Psalters does not coincide exactly with the counting in previous Psalters, for where the rubrics place the 14th verse at "The waters became thick", current Psalters place the 14th verse at "The enemy said", and "The waters became thick" moves to the 15th verse. The 6th Ode has only 12 verses, so do not forget to divide these two verses of it on 4. The 9th Ode, one, of the Theotokos, is sung whole before the heirmos with "More honorable", and the other, of Zachariah, is sung whole in the refrains, and in those editions where there are only 13 verses, one verse must be divided into 2.

provenance.verbatim_source: Regarding the refrains to the troparia of the canon, know that in order to find the number of refrains as quickly as possible, the last four, six, and eight verses of the Biblical Odes (except the 2nd, for it is read in full before the heirmos) from the bottom up are marked in the middle of the song, or on the side, with the inscription: "on 4, on 6, on 8". But on 14 they are not counted off, since 6 verses from 8 upwards are easily counted. However, the counting of 14 verses in current Psalters does not coincide exactly with the counting in previous Psalters, for where the rubrics place the 14th verse at "The waters became thick", current Psalters place the 14th verse at "The enemy said", and "The waters became thick" moves to the 15th verse. The 6th Ode has only 12 verses, so do not forget to divide these two verses of it on 4. The 9th Ode, one, of the Theotokos, is sung whole before the heirmos with "More honorable", and the other, of Zachariah, is sung whole in the refrains, and in those editions where there are only 13 verses, one verse must be divided into 2.

units.english_text: On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of the first week of Great Lent, after "O come, let us worship", we recite Psalm 69 "O God, come to my assistance", given in the order of Great Compline after the 3rd "O come, let us worship", after the prayer "O Master God the Father"; then one fourth part of each ode of the Great Canon (Matins on Thursday before the 5th Sunday of Lent)[^524]. Refrain to the troparia of the canon – "Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me"[^525], to the troparion of St. Mary of Egypt – "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us", and to the troparion of St. Andrew – "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us". According to the rubric, 3 small prostrations should be made at each troparion of the canon, however, among us this is not done, since there are no people in church at that time

units.english_text: On Wednesday we make 3 small prostrations: at the Trisagion at the beginning, at "O come, let us worship", at "Alleluia" after the pre-introductory psalm and after each antiphon of the Kathisma and at "Let my prayer be set forth". Great prostrations, according to local custom, we make at "Light of Christ", when the Priest blesses the people crosswise with the triple-candle; at the conclusion of the singing "Let my prayer be set forth" and after "Now the Powers of Heaven", when the consecrated Lamb is taken from the artophorion and placed on the diskos[^526]. And on Fridays at Vespers and at Compline we do not make prostrations, only the prescribed ones at the Presanctified, that is: after "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations[^527], after the Entrance of the Holy Gifts – 3 prostrations and at "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations, and among us also at "Light of Christ" – 3 prostrations.

Great prostrations, according to local custom, we make at "Light of Christ", when the Priest blesses the people crosswise with the triple-candle; at the conclusion of the singing "Let my prayer be set forth" and after "Now the Powers of Heaven", when the consecrated Lamb is taken from the artophorion and placed on the diskos[^526]. And on Fridays at Vespers and at Compline we do not make prostrations, only the prescribed ones at the Presanctified, that is: after "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations[^527], after the Entrance of the Holy Gifts – 3 prostrations and at "Let my prayer be set forth" – 3 prostrations, and among us also at "Light of Christ" – 3 prostrations.

units.english_text: 7. "Let my prayer be set forth". Has after it three verses and is sung six times, that is: twice – before the first verse, once – after each verse and again once at the end. And among us the first time "Let my prayer be set forth" is sung by the Priest, the second time – by the Choir, all three verses – by the Priest, after each the Choir – "Let my prayer be set forth", the last time in a higher voice up to the half – the Priest, and from the half – the Choir. Where there are two choirs, they sing "Let my prayer be set forth" alternately: the first begins after the Priest, and the second half is sung by both choirs together. When the Priest sings, he himself stands, and the Choir and people kneel; when the Choir sings, the Choir stands together with the people, and the Priest kneels. If there are two choirs, the one singing stands, and the other kneels; people who are on the side of the right choir kneel, stand and sing with the right choir, and those on the left – with the left[^531].

units.english_text: The Priest sings "Let my prayer be set forth" first in front of the altar, then the 1st verse – on the south, the 2nd – on the west, the 3rd – on the north side, and at the end the first half – again in front of the holy table[^532]. He censes each side of the altar twice, that is before the beginning of his singing and at the end of the Choir's singing, that is at "The lifting up of my hands", for then, having censed, he moves to the next side of the altar, in order to cense there also, so that the Choir is ready to sing its verse[^533].

units.english_text: If there is no Liturgy of the Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric of Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, that is from the 10 stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* we transfer the first 3 to the Aposticha, and the other 6 we sing on *“Lord, I have cried”*[^534]; and there will be on Wednesday stichera of the *Triodion* – 3 and of the *Menaion* – 3, and on Friday Martyria of the *Octoechos* – 3 and of the *Menaion* – 3. On Friday evening, after "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", there will be no Lenten troparia with prostrations, but the Troparion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint and, after the litany "Have mercy on us, O God", – 3 great prostrations[^535] and the Great Dismissal, as usual

units.english_text: If on this day falls a saint with Polyeleos, namely the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner and the 40 Martyrs, and also on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week[^536], then immediately after "Let my prayer be set forth" there will be censing and on the two previously named feasts their Epistle and Gospel are read, the Gospel – beginning from "Wisdom, Aright". On the three days of Passion Week only the Gospel is read, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy", since there is no Epistle

units.english_text: Compline on all Fridays of Great Lent, according to the Greek rubric, is Small, and according to the Pochaiv *Triodion*, *Tserkovne Oko* and the Moscow Typikon – Great. However, in our times, when abbreviations prevail, we should adhere to the Greek rubric, the more so because even in our Horologia, in the order of Great Compline, troparia are given only for 4 days of the week, that is for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. We do not make prostrations, as was already said on page 349.

units.english_text: we sing the Canon for the Dead, which is in the *Octoechos* for the current tone, and the Canons of the *Menaion* to the saints of the nearest Saturday and Sunday we sing, if the Ecclesiarch prefers, one – at Compline on Friday with the Canon for the Dead, and the other – on Sunday at Compline[^540]. The Greek *Triodion* adds: "we do so on all Friday evenings of holy and Great Lent". Before the Canon for the Dead we should sing also the usual Theotokion Canon of the *Octoechos*, for the rubric does not exclude it[^541]

units.english_text: Let it be known that from this Monday of the 2nd week of Lent the canons of the saints in the *Menaion*, which fall from the Saturday of Lazarus to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, are sung at Compline with the Theotokion Canons. First the Canon of the Theotokos is sung, and after it – the Canon of the *Menaion*. After the 3rd Ode – Kontakion and Sessional Hymn of the *Menaion*, and after the 6th – Sessional Hymn of the Theotokos; after the canon – Stichera of the *Menaion* (*Triodion* of this day).

units.english_text: The service of this Saturday, as also the services of the 3rd and 4th Saturdays of Great Lent, differ from the services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost in that it does not exclude fully either the service of the *Menaion*, or the service of the day of the *Octoechos*, that is to all saints and the dead. The services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost exclude generally the service of the *Menaion*, and from the service of the *Octoechos* little is taken, but have their own order in the *Triodion* exclusively for the dead. Therefore, we suppose that the two litanies for the dead: "In peace let us pray to the Lord" and "Have mercy on us, O God", which according to our later rubric are given at Vespers and at Matins, and the litany for the dead "Again and again", which is said between the odes of the canon, should be taken only on these two Saturdays which are exclusively for the dead, and on the other three – usual litanies.

units.english_text: 5. **Canons:** *Distribution:* Canons 3 on 14: of the Temple of the Lord or Theotokos with heirmos on 6, of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 4 and of the *Octoechos* of the current tone the second[^547] on 4. If the Temple is of a Saint, then – Canon of the Saint with heirmos on 6, Temple on 4 and Octoechos on 4. From the 6th Ode, leaving the Canons of the Temple and Octoechos, we sing the Canon of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 6 and both canons of the tetraodion on 8. Refrain to the troparia of the tetraodion – "Holy Martyrs, pray to God for us". At the end of the eight troparia of each ode of the tetraodion we add two more troparia: one Martyric with the Martyric refrain, and the second – for the dead with the refrain for the dead. From the two Martyric refrains "Wondrous is God" and "To the saints that are in His earth" and from the two refrains for the dead "Their souls" and "Blessed are they Whom Thou Hast chosen", the first we refrain to the Martyric and for the dead of the 6th and 8th Odes, and the second – to the Martyric and for the dead of the 7th and 9th Odes.

If the Temple is of a Saint, then – Canon of the Saint with heirmos on 6, Temple on 4 and Octoechos on 4. From the 6th Ode, leaving the Canons of the Temple and Octoechos, we sing the Canon of the Saint of the *Menaion* on 6 and both canons of the tetraodion on 8. At the end of the eight troparia of each ode of the tetraodion we add two more troparia: one Martyric with the Martyric refrain, and the second – for the dead with the refrain for the dead. units.english_text: After the dismissal of the Liturgy, and also after the end of every service celebrated in church, from this day until the end of the 6th Hour of the following Friday, veneration of the Precious Cross takes place: the Priest, having come before the tetrapod, sings together with the people "Before Thy Cross we bow down" (3). If there be a sufficient number of people, the Choir sings the stichera of veneration until all have venerated, according to the rubric given on page 127, in the note[^549].

units.english_text: Everything – according to the general Lenten rubric of the previous weeks, except the veneration of the Precious Cross, according to the previously stated. Only Wednesday and Friday differ from the other three days in that at Matins, instead of the Canon of the *Menaion*, they have the Cross Canon of the *Triodion*. Also at Vespers on Tuesday for Wednesday all 6 stichera on *“Lord, I have cried”* will be of the Cross; and the Canon of the *Menaion* on these two days we take at Compline.

units.english_text: The service of St. John of the Ladder, which some later [typika] prescribed to sing on this Sunday, is usually not taken among us. And if someone, namely in monasteries, wishes to sing it, let him sing it instead of the service of the regular saint of the *Menaion*, according to the rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on 4, and let him take the service of the regular saint at Compline. According to this Typikon, the service of St. Mary of Egypt is sung on the fifth[^550] Sunday of Lent, but if someone wishes, he may sing it instead of the service of the regular saint.

units.english_text: 1. From the beginning to the end of the Sessional Hymns of the *Octoechos*, given at the end of the *Triodion*, at the 1st Kathisma, we sing everything according to the general Lenten rubric, then Psalm 50 and immediately, having omitted the litany "Save, O God", the Great Canon[^551]. At the time of the singing of the canon the holy doors are opened and candles are lit on the holy table. Before the holy doors in cathedral churches a rug is spread, on which first the Bishop, if he be present, and then the other sacred ministers two by two, according to the rank of their dignity, at each ode make one great prostration, after the singing of each troparion of the ode of the canon. In our seminary, the seminarians make prostrations before the holy doors, and in the sanctuary, before the steps of the altar, all eight superiors make prostrations according to the rank of their dignity, one at one ode, by turn, and at the 9th Ode – all eight together, in epitrachelia

units.english_text: 2. **Canons:** Canons two: one – the Great [Canon] of St. Andrew, of nine odes, the second – triodion, contains the 4th, 8th and 9th Odes, which also in these odes takes the first place. The odes of the nine-ode canon do not have an equal number of troparia and each of them has at the end two troparia to St. Mary of Egypt and one to St. Andrew of Crete. The triodion we sing on 10 troparia with the first heirmos, for the 2nd heirmos is not sung. Refrains to the troparia of the Great Canon are these: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", then "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us", then "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us". To the troparia of the triodion the refrain will be – "Holy Apostles, pray to God for us"[^552], because according to content they belong to the service of Thursday. At each troparion of the Canon of St. Andrew the rubrics prescribe three prostrations, but we make only one, however, great, and in cathedral temples the clergy makes prostrations only by turn and adapted to the nine odes of the canon. The choirs sing the canon in the middle of the church, each at a separate analogion, making at the troparia of the canon a small prostration. As Katavasia at all odes we take the heirmos of the last canon[^553]

units.english_text: The service of this feast is of the small type; it has only the Katavasia at Matins after each ode and the Great Doxology and is combined with the usual service of Lenten Saturday and with the Temple Canon at Matins. The peculiarity of this feast lies in that at its Matins the whole order of the Akathist to the Most Pure Virgin Mary is sung, the 12 ikos-Kontakia of which are divided into four quarters, the first of which is sung instead of the Sessional Hymn after the first Kathisma, the second – instead of the Sessional Hymn – after the second Kathisma, the third – after the 3rd, and the fourth – after the 6th Ode of the Canon; the initial Kontakion is sung at the beginning and at the end of each quarter, and before the last singing of it – once more the first Ikos[^556]. This Matins, according to the rubric, is sung at the 4th hour of the night, but we sing it at the usual time[^557]. The service of the regular saint, according to the rubric of the Greek *Triodion*, is sung at Compline.

units.english_text: This Akathist order is celebrated usually at the altar. In the cathedral temple it is sung at the altar of the Mother of God, which is located in its right nave; and then the Priest censes the altar and everything else, as usual, and immediately, having left the holy doors open, goes out through them to the altar of the Most Holy Theotokos and sings there the Akathist order, censing from the altar at the beginning of each quarter the icon of the Mother of God, the sacred ministers, the choirs and the people. After singing the 4th quarter of the ikos-Kontakia the Priest returns to the sanctuary, closes the holy doors and goes to the sacristy, where he takes off the sacred vestments and, having put on the epitrachelion, continues the service of Matins.

units.english_text: The service of this feast is of the small type and only at Matins, from the Canon onwards, – great. units.english_text: 2. The blessing and distribution of branches takes place, according to the rubric, immediately after the 50th Psalm, during the kissing of the Gospel. According to our custom, the blessing takes place after the 50th Psalm, and the distribution – during the anointing with oil (myrovanie), that is during the canon. And it takes place thus: When the Priest has sung the Gospel, he places it on the analogion near the tetrapod, between two candles lit on candlesticks. On the tetrapod are placed branches and prepared censers and sprinklers. The Priest approaches the tetrapod and at the time when the Choir reads the 50th Psalm, having put incense in and blessed the censer, censes the branches from the four sides of the tetrapod and, after the conclusion of the 50th Psalm, when the Deacon exclaims (if there be none, then the Priest himself) "Let us pray to the Lord", reads aloud (from the *Sluzhebnik* (lit. "Sluzhebnik") or from the *Triodion*[^563] ) the first prayer "O Lord our God", and the Choir responds: "Amen". Priest: "Peace be to all"; deacon: "Bow your heads unto the Lord"; and, after "To Thee, O Lord", the Priest reads the second prayer "O Lord God Almighty... unto ages of ages"[^564]; choir: "Amen"; the Priest sprinkles the branches with holy water, saying: "These branches are blessed and sanctified" and the rest; and, after singing the litany "Save, O God", with His right hand anoints the people, and with His left hand distributes to all the branches, which the Deacon solemnly hands to him, and if there be no deacon, then one of the church servers[^565]

units.english_text: 2. Immediately after the Theotokion "O Theotokos, Thou Art the vine" at the 3rd Hour and, after the corresponding Theotokia, at the other two Hours, the rubrics prescribe the reading of the Four Gospels, which today among us is read only in cathedral, or conciliar, churches[^573]. At the 6th Hour we read the Gospel not immediately after the Theotokion, but after the conclusion of the Troparion of the Prophecy and the Paremia with its Prokimena. The reading of the Four Gospels covers all the Evangelists, that is Matthew, Mark and Luke in full, and John – only up to the "Passion of Christ", that is up to "Now is the Son of man glorified", Section 46, verse 13.32. All the Evangelists, taken together, are divided into 9 readings, according to the number of the three Hours (3, 6, 9) and three days (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday). Matthew is divided into 2 readings, Mark – into 2, John – into 2, and Luke – into 3. The first reading covers the first half of Matthew, the second – the second half of Matthew, the third – the first half of Mark, the fourth – the second half of Mark, the fifth – the first part of Luke, the sixth – the second part of Luke, the seventh – the third part of Luke, the eighth – the first half of John, the ninth – the second half of John. The rubric does not indicate where the first half of the three Evangelists and the first and second parts of Luke end. But since Matthew has 28 chapters, its half ends with the 14th chapter, Mark – 16 chapters, so its half ends with the 8th chapter, Luke – 24 chapters, so its first part ends with the 8th chapter, and the second – with the 16th. John, up to "Now is [the Son of man] glorified", has 12 chapters and part of the 13th chapter, therefore its half ends with the 6th chapter and part of the 7th

units.english_text: The Priest, at the beginning of each reading, dressed in a phelonion of Lenten color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual, then, having come out through the holy doors to the analogion placed before the holy doors facing the people, on which stand two candlesticks with lit candles, reads from there the Gospel, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy". After the conclusion of each reading, having kissed the beginning of the reading and leaving the Gospel on the analogion until the end of the 3rd reading, he returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors, takes off the phelonion[^574].

After the conclusion of each reading, having kissed the beginning of the reading and leaving the Gospel on the analogion until the end of the 3rd reading, he returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors, takes off the phelonion[^574].

units.english_text: "It is fitting for the Priest on Great Thursday at the Liturgy to consecrate two Lambs, in order to consume one at Communion, and to place the other in the artophorion and keep in the tabernacle in the usual place until today (Friday)". Thus in our *Sluzhebnik*[^584]. Regarding the Lamb itself, which is to be kept in the tabernacle until the day of exposition, the Synod of Lviv orders that "it before consecration be fitted to its vessel, the so-called Melchizedek, into which it is well inserted and carefully wiped, so that afterwards crumbs do not fall from it; so that placed in such a way in the Melchizedek, it be consecrated at the Liturgy of one of the preceding days and kept in the tabernacle until the exposition itself". When the Priest prepares the Lamb at the Proskomedia, wishing to use it for exposition, he does not say over it the words "In remembrance of the Lord" etc., nor does He perform over it the sacred actions which are usually performed over the Lamb that is to be consumed at the same Divine Service, for it is considered only communicative; it is enough only to cut it, so that it would be convenient to break and consume it on another day.

Between the troparion and the canon there will be five Sessional Hymns, each of which has before it three antiphons of the Passion troparia, without Kathismata and small litanies, then the Beatitudes, Prokimenon and Psalm 50. Besides this we read 12 Passion Gospels: the first – after the troparion, the five following – after each of the five Sessional Hymns, the seventh – after the Beatitudes, the eighth – after the 50th Psalm, the ninth – after the Exaposteilarion, the tenth – after the Praises, the eleventh – after "Let us complete", the twelfth – after the Aposticha. After the singing of each Gospel we ring all the church bells and, after the twelfth Gospel, we do not ring until the Resurrection itself, but instead of bells we use wooden clappers. But it is better already at Passion Matins not to ring, but to strike clappers or boards, for Passion Matins is a time of sorrow, to which the joyful sounds of bells do not correspond. Also in Rome already at Passion Matins clappers are used.

units.english_text: All this – exactly so at the readings of the other Gospels, with the exception of the litany and censing, which according to the rubric of our Triodia and the Typikon of the Lviv University, will be only at the 1st Gospel and at the five Sessional Hymns, and the censing – only of the holy table. They give thus: "We do not sit at these Sessional Hymns, since the Priest censes the holy table, but we sing them standing"[^588]. Finally we consider that it is fitting to cense not only at the Sessional Hymns, but also at all other Gospels, for the censing takes place not for the sake of the Sessional Hymns, but for the sake of the Gospels, however, only the holy table (around), as our Triodia have, which mention the censing only of the holy table. Everything should be censed only twice, that is at the 1st Gospel and at the Canon, at the heirmos of the 9th Ode.

units.english_text: If there be deacons, they remain from the beginning of Matins, dressed in dalmatic with orarion of violet color, in the sanctuary, at their places, until they begin to sing the third time the troparion "When the glorious disciples"; then they come out together with the Priest who will sing the Gospel, dressed in a violet phelonion, before the steps of the altar and, having bowed together with him to the Holy Mysteries, open the holy doors, cense everything as usual, as at the beginning of the Liturgy, return before the steps of the altar and, having given up the censers and bowed both together to the Holy Mysteries, go out, each through his door, before the holy doors and, again having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, stand there until the second deacon after the singing of the troparion sings the Small Litany; then, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries and having exchanged their places, they proceed to the analogion so that, when the Priest approaches the analogion, the first Deacon is on the right, and the second – on the left of him. When the Priest, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, comes out through the holy doors to the analogion, the first Deacon exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy". Priest: "Peace be to all". Second deacon: "Wisdom, Aright. Let us listen". Priest: "The Reading from (Name)". First deacon: "Let us attend". Priest – reading. After the conclusion of the reading, the Priest kisses the beginning of the reading first himself, afterwards the Deacon who is on the right kisses [it], and after him the one who is on the left. All three return to the sanctuary: the Priest – through the central, and the deacons – through the side doors, stand together with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having closed the holy doors and bowed all together to the Holy Mysteries, go to their places. At the other Gospels, since there will be no Small Litany, the deacons, having come out before the holy doors, bow and, having exchanged places, proceed to the analogion and, when the Priest stands between them, exclaim: "And that we may be accounted worthy" and the rest, as above.

units.english_text: On Friday morning, before the beginning of the Royal Hours, the Shroud and the most beautiful Book of the Holy Gospels is placed on the holy table. Before the holy doors is placed the Tomb of God, at which, according to the custom of the northern and western Latin churches[^598], the Holy Mysteries are exposed until the Resurrection of Christ itself. Our Sluzhebnyky prescribe placing on this Tomb the Artophorion with the Holy Mysteries. According to the custom of our archcathedral temple, the Holy Mysteries are exposed in a monstrance on the main altar. And the Tomb of God should be erected so that above it rises a cross without the Crucified One, with a cloth hung on its crossbar and with the instruments of Christ's passion, it should be decorated with costly carpets, surrounded by many candlesticks and lamps and vessels with small trees and flowers. The front board of the sarcophagus is covered with red damask, to which a cloth is attached, and to it afterwards the Shroud will be attached. The board itself should not lie horizontally, but slanted so that the Shroud attached to it would be visible and accessible for veneration.

units.english_text: The sacred ministers, the Bishop and the four most worthy canons, who will carry the Shroud, vest in all sacred vestments of their rank, and the other canons and priests – only in epitrachelia and phelonia, some – only in epitrachelia, and two deacons – in all diaconal [vestments]. Lit candles are distributed to the canons and other priests in the sanctuary, and to the brotherhood – in the church. The sacred ministers approach the steps of the altar and bow low. The Bishop ascends to the altar, takes the Shroud, spread on the altar, and gives it to the four canons so that each holds it by one corner. Then the Deacon who is on the right ascends to the altar and, having bowed low, unlocks the artophorion, takes from there the pyx with the Holy Mysteries, places [it] on the (folded) antimension, takes from there the Lamb with the stand into which it is inserted, not touching it with his fingers, but holding by the stand, places [it] into the monstrance and locks it well. Having locked the pyx, he places [it] into the artophorion and, having bowed, locks it also; and places the monstrance on the antimension so that it faces the people, steps aside until the Bishop, kneeling, censes the Holy Mysteries three times, each time – with a prostration at the end, and, having taken upon himself the omophorion (aer), approaches the altar. Then the Deacon, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, takes with both hands the monstrance and hands it to the Bishop, who before that makes a prostration. The Bishop turns to the right to the people, and when the singers begin to sing "Thee, Who Art clothed with light", goes out behind the clergy through the holy doors on the northern side of the Tomb into the church and, having entered under the canopy, surrounded by candle-bearers and preceded by two deacons who cense unceasingly, proceeds behind all to the church doors. In front goes the cross-bearer, then the banner-bearers, four girls icon-bearers, after them – the church brotherhood, the seminarians, the seminary choir, then, from the holy doors, – priests, canons, four sacred dignitaries who carry the Shroud, turned with feet to the people, and at the end – the Bishop with deacons who cense, and candle-bearers. The procession goes out of the church and turns to the right, that is to its northern side and, having gone around the church three times (or, as now they do there, – once), returns to the church. Those who carry the Shroud, and the other priests stand before the Tomb, and the Bishop with the deacons returns by the southern side of the Tomb, through the holy doors, to the sanctuary. The right deacon receives from his hands the Holy Mysteries and places [them] on the altar. The Bishop kneels and, having put aside the omophorion (Velum), censes the Holy Mysteries three times, each time bowing his head; the Deacon, having bowed, exposes the Holy Mysteries at the top of the tabernacle. Having bowed before the steps of the altar, all three depart: the Bishop through the central, the deacons – through the side doors before the Tomb. The Bishop receives the Shroud from the canons who hold it, and places [it] on the Tomb, and they fasten it to the Tomb. When the singers have finished singing "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", the Trisagion and the rest with "Our Father", the Bishop exclaims: "For Thine is the Kingdom" and begins to sing with the servers the troparion "The noble Joseph"; at the end he makes with the servers a low bow, and all the people – a great prostration to the ground. Then the second time the same troparion – the second choir, and all – a prostration, as before. And where there will be only one choir, the first time the troparion is sung by the sacred ministers, the second time – by the Choir, the third time the half – by the sacred ministers, and from "wrapped [it]" and further – by the Choir[^601]. After the singing of the troparion and after the prostrations all kiss the Shroud, according to the order, having made before the kissing one prostration: first the Bishop, and after him – all other sacred ministers, according to the rank of their dignity. After this there will be the Great Dismissal, specific to this Saturday, after which the sacred ministers return to the sanctuary, leaving the holy doors open until the end of Bright Week, take off the sacred vestments and go out, and the people kiss the Shroud[^602].

units.english_text: The Entrance takes place thus: During the singing of the Stichera of the Praises the Priest and deacons, if there be any, having bowed low before the Shroud, and simultaneously also before the Holy Mysteries, go to the sacristy and vest in all sacred vestments of their rank. During the singing of the Doxastikon also the other sacred ministers, who are before the Tomb of God, dressed in phelonia, having bowed low, depart to the sanctuary and, when the Priest with the deacons comes before the steps of the altar, stand together with him on both sides and bow all together to the Holy Mysteries. After singing the Praises [Stichera] the Priest exclaims: "Glory to Thee Who Hast shown us the light", then puts incense in for the left deacon and, when the Doxology ends, approaches the altar, takes from it the Gospel, gives it to the right deacon and, preceded by candle-bearers and the Deacon with the censer, they make the Entrance just as at the Liturgy. Having stood before the Tomb of God: the right deacon – on the right, and the left – on the left of the Priest, closer to the Tomb, the other sacred ministers – on two wings, a little at a distance, await the conclusion of the Trisagion and the sticheron "Come, let us bless". After the conclusion of the singing of the sticheron the first deacon, raising the orarion in the direction of the people, exclaims: "Let us attend", the Priest, blessing the people: "Peace be to all", the second deacon, raising the orarion: "Wisdom, let us attend" and we sing the Troparion "The noble Joseph" once. The first deacon places the Gospel on the analogion facing the people, the second gives up the censer and the Troparion of the Prophecy once[^607].

units.english_text: Regarding the time and place of the placing of the Shroud we do not find an ancient rubric, for this rite is later and different in different regions. According to the custom of our archcathedral church the Shroud remains hung behind the holy table, over the High Place, from Resurrection Matins to the Apodosis of the Resurrection inclusive, that is until Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of our other churches, the Shroud, taken from the Tomb before Resurrection Matins, is placed on the holy table, where it remains during the whole Bright Week, and from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Apodosis of the Resurrection – behind the holy table. According to others – it remains on the altar, the antimension with the Gospel is placed on it and the Liturgy is celebrated on it. However, it is better to place the Shroud behind the holy table, for lying on the altar, it is often significantly damaged by candles, from which wax drips on it.

units.english_text: After the Shroud is taken from the Tomb of God and transferred to the sanctuary, the sacred ministers, having dressed in all the brightest sacred vestments of their rank, go out before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all together low to the Holy Mysteries, bend their knees and receive lit candles; so also the brotherhood in the church. The Deacon, who is on the right (or the Priest himself, if there be no deacons) approaches the middle of the altar and, having bowed low, places the Gospel on its right side, then, having taken the Holy Mysteries from the tabernacle and placed them on the antimension, steps aside a little, and the Bishop (or main priest), having censed the Holy Mysteries three times, as usual, and having taken upon himself the omophorion, rises, ascends the steps and, having bowed, receives the Holy Mysteries, after which turns to the people and begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior". Under the joyful sound of all bells the procession around the church takes place, with everything, as was given on Great Friday at Vespers, here on page 394, except the Shroud, which now, by the decision of bl. m. Cardinal Sembratovych, should not be carried, for this does not correspond to the joy of the Resurrection; rather it is fitting to carry the icon of the Resurrection, as it is in the *Triodion*, at the beginning of Resurrection Matins, during the procession to the church doors. Therefore, when the main sacred minister begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior", the choirs and people take up the singing and sing it, repeating, all the time, until the procession ends, namely the circuit of the church either three times, or at least once. When the circuit ends, all enter the church; in order, however, to avoid confusion during the second procession, those carrying banners and icons remain before the church doors, and in the church prepare for the procession the cross-bearer with two candle-bearers, the brotherhood, choirs and clergy. When the sacred ministers enter the sanctuary, the main priest ascends to the altar and, having turned to the people, blesses them with the Holy Mysteries, quietly saying: "Save, O God, Thy people and bless Thine inheritance", places the Holy Mysteries on the altar, descends before the steps, bends the knees and, having taken off the omophorion, censes the Holy Mysteries three times, as usual; the Deacon, having approached the Holy Mysteries, bows low, takes them with the stand from the monstrance and places into the artophorion, and places the artophorion into the tabernacle and, having bowed, locks it. And where there will be no monstrance, the Holy Mysteries are placed in the artophorion and with it are locked in the tabernacle.

units.english_text: PROCESSION BEFORE THE CHURCH DOORS. All people go out of the church, and after them go out also the sacred ministers. And the procession takes place thus: All sacred ministers, in all their sacred bright vestments, stand before the steps of the altar. The main sacred minister takes the cross, the Deacon – the censer, all together bow low to the Holy Mysteries and turn to the west. The main one begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior", all take up the singing of the sticheron and go out from the sanctuary to the church: the Priest – through the holy [doors], and all other sacred ministers – through the Deacon's doors; at this time all bells ring, and all go to the great church doors and, having gone out of the church, stand according to rank before the church doors, which are immediately closed[^615]. In the middle of the church is placed on the holy table first of all the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, usually on the Artos, also other holy icons, reliquaries and the book of the Holy Gospels in the most precious binding or something else of the sacred things, all this – according to the number of priests who will give them to be kissed by the people at the end of Matins. Outside, before the church doors, Matins begins in the following way[^616]

units.english_text: BEGINNING OF MATINS. Immediately after the church doors are closed, the main priest, holding with his left hand the cross, and with his right – the censer and censing the church doors[^617], exclaims loudly: "Glory to the Holy" and the rest. The Choir responds: "Amen"; the Priest gives up the censer and sings loudly the troparion "Christ is risen", also all – the same, then the Priest the second time – the same and all – the same, and the third time the Priest – the same and all – the same, then the Priest in a high voice exclaims the verses, and all after each verse sing this troparion once[^618]. At the end the Priest, having sung in a higher voice the same troparion only up to "trampling down death by death" inclusive, opens the doors, and all finish: "and upon those in the tombs bestowing life" and again all bells ring, all enter the church[^619]. The Matins prayers at Resurrection Matins throughout the whole Bright Week are not recited, for they are connected with the Six Psalms, and since there will be no Six Psalms here, there will be no prayers. If it were necessary to recite the prayers, it should be indicated in the rubric where they should be recited, for during the verses "Let God arise", which take the place of the Six Psalms, it is not possible to recite them, for at this time the rubric orders the Priest to sing verses, and not to add prayers as well

If there be many people, then we begin the kissing not after the stichera of the Resurrection, but from their beginning, that is from the verse "Let God arise". If there be very many people, then the kissing will be also during the canon. And this kissing takes place thus:

units.english_text: If there be only one priest, he stands in the holy doors and from there gives the cross to be kissed by the people, greeting everyone: "Christ is risen", and the one Who kisses answers: "Truly He is risen". If there be several priests, then first the main one goes out from the holy doors and stands before the iconostasis, on the right side, that is opposite the icon of the Savior, looking to the north. After Him the second priest comes out from the holy doors with the Gospel, approaches the main one, and he gives him the cross to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", having kissed, in His turn, gives Him the Gospel to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen" and stands on His left. Then comes out the third priest with the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, approaches the first and He gives Him the cross to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and having kissed gives Him the icon of the Resurrection to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen", and approaches the second priest, who gives him the Gospel to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and He, having kissed the Gospel, gives the second to kiss the icon of the Resurrection, answering: "Truly He is risen", and stands on the left of the second. The fourth priest comes out with the icon of the Theotokos, approaches the first, also the second and the third, of whom each gives him his object to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and having kissed gives each of them the icon of the Theotokos to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen". So do also all other priests, as many as there be. In cathedral churches the Bishop, sitting on his throne opposite the icon of the Savior, gives the cross to be kissed, also each of the canons gives His insignia to be kissed, sitting on the seat. And when the kissing between the priests ends, then other sacred ministers and all the people approach one by one each Priest in turn, starting from the first, and kiss his insignia, answering: "Truly He is risen"[^622]. After the kissing once was read the "Homily" of Chrysostom, which is in the Flower *Triodion*.

units.english_text: Also at "With the fear of God", instead of "Blessed is He that cometh" and instead of "We have seen the true light", we sing "Christ is risen" once. Instead of "Let our mouths be filled" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" – "Christ is risen" (3)[^626]. Among us usually "Christ is risen" is recited also instead of "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens", however, this violates the memory of the mystery of Christ's Ascension, which is mentioned in this place of the Liturgy from the beginning. Our priests say "Christ is risen" (only these two words) also after "With the fear of God", after "Save, O God" and after "Always, now and ever", however, in no rubric do we find this.

units.english_text: Our Sluzhebnyky: "If served conciliarly, then this Gospel is read by all priests and deacons by verses as the Superior decides". About this you have a detailed rubric in our and Russian Triodia. However, the custom that one and the same Gospel be read by all priests and deacons – is a superfluous invention of the Greco-Slavs, which today takes place among us only when the Gospel is read in different languages, as happens in our cathedral temples, in which the Bishop reads it in Greek from the holy doors, then the Deacon – in Slavonic from the ambo, and at the end canons and priests, placed throughout the whole church, in different liturgical languages. In Russia the Bishop reads the Gospel in Slavonic, and other priests – in Hebrew, in Greek and in Latin, in those languages in which the inscription on the Cross was written, then in other new languages (Muralt. 14. Brief. S. 142). The Greeks also read the Gospel, according to the new custom, in different languages, however, not at the Liturgy, but at Vespers (the Gospel read at Vespers of this day), as happens in the Patriarchate of Constantinople[^628].

units.english_text: 7. BLESSING OF THE ARTOS. After the Prayer behind the Ambo[^629] takes place the blessing of the Artos, for which you have the prayer in the *Sluzhebnik* after the Liturgy of the Resurrection; after the prayer the Artos is sprinkled with holy water. And this Artos with the feast, that is the icon of the Resurrection, after the dismissal of the Liturgy, is carried from the altar, on which it was blessed, to the tetrapod, where it remains until Bright Saturday and the faithful entering the church kiss it. On Bright Saturday at the Liturgy, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, the Priest, having come out through the holy doors, reads over it the prayer for breaking, given only in our *Sluzhebnik* on Bright Saturday, and after this, it is taken from the tetrapod, broken in the sacristy and on the next day, that is on the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, is distributed to the faithful by the Priest standing in the holy doors[^630]

units.english_text: To the divine service from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Ascension one could apply the general rule in the middle of a feast of the Lord. However, since each Sunday, beginning from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, has a separate name and a separate service, which extends to the other weekdays of the given week and is as if a separate feast in the Easter time, the place of the Resurrection service is taken by the service of the Sunday, also on weekdays, together with some parts of the Sunday service of the *Octoechos*, except the eight-day feast of Mid-Pentecost, to which the Sunday service yields on weekdays. units.english_text: This feast is of the Lord, of eight days, which is commemorated on the Wednesday of the Paralytic and ends on the Wednesday of the Samaritan Woman, on which it is leavetaken. On the feast itself and on the Apodosis only the service of the feast is sung, and the service of the regular saint of the *Menaion* is sung at Compline; on other days – it is combined with the *Menaion*, except the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman, for then it is combined with the service of the Sunday. This feast has no All-Night Vigil, nor Polyeleos at Matins, only the Great Doxology, and at Vespers – both Entrance and readings. We begin its service on Tuesday evening, for the liturgical day begins in the evening of the preceding day.

units.english_text: Feast, Afterfeast and Apodosis of the feast – according to the general rule of a feast of the Lord, only at the Liturgy our Sluzhebnyky, instead of "We have seen" and "Let our mouths be filled", give the verse "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens, and Thy glory over all the earth" and so we take until the Apodosis; on the following Sunday, of the Holy Fathers, the service of the Ascension has a specific rubric, for it is combined both with the Sunday service, and of the Holy Fathers, as is given below.

units.english_text: The service of this feast is celebrated for seven days, for it is leavetaken on the following Saturday. And it has this peculiarity, that on Sunday evening at Vespers for Monday prayers with bending of knees are read, and in the morning, that is on Monday the whole service of the feast is sung, without the *Menaion*, and at the Liturgy – also the service of the Holy Trinity, if desired[^654], as we will note immediately. Everything else, from the feast to its Apodosis, is celebrated according to the general rule of the feast, in the middle of a feast of the Lord. At the Liturgy "All Who have been baptized into Christ" – only on the feast itself

units.english_text: The prayers with bending of knees are read in three places of Vespers: after the Great Prokimenon, after "Let us all say" and after "Vouchsafe, O Lord". At each of these three stations of prayers the Small Litany is sung, each time with a separate exclamation, however, thus: "Lord, have mercy" (3), then the Priest – one station of prayers with bending of knees; at the end of the station the Deacon or priest continues the Small Litany, that is: "Help us, save us, have mercy", "Commemorating our most holy, most pure", exclamation. So – at each station.

units.english_text: This fast begins on Monday after the Sunday of All Saints, and ends on the Eve of the feast of the Holy Apostles. Regarding the divine service on this, first, Monday, if a saint with Polyeleos does not fall, "Alleluia" was sung once and the whole church rule was Lenten, as on Lenten days of Great Lent; however, now we limit "Alleluia" to Great Lent, and here we sing *“God is the Lord”*.

units.english_text: This feast lasts eight days: from Thursday after the Sunday of All Saints to the next [Thursday], on which it is leavetaken. But since, according to our custom, it is transferred from Thursday to the following Sunday, the Synod of Lviv orders to sing the service of this feast on Sunday, with All-Night Vigil, exactly as given in the *Triodion* on Thursday of the feast itself, according to the general rubric of a feast of the Lord of the first rank, without the Sunday [service]; and on the days preceding and following this Sunday, to sing it according to the general rubric in the middle of a feast of the Lord. Besides this, the Synod orders that the procession with the Holy Mysteries take place on the Sunday itself, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, as usual, that is from the church to four altars, erected outside the church and equally distant from one another. Where this would be impossible, it will be sufficient to begin the procession from the altar in the church and, having gone around the church three times, to end this rite on the same altar in the church with the blessing with the Holy Mysteries. Regarding the four readings of the Gospel, which are usually sung at each of the four altars, the Synod orders to choose those in which there is mention of the Most Holy Mysteries, according to the rubric prescribed for this feast[^661].

units.english_text: The Priest, on one of the days preceding the feast, let him consecrate at the Liturgy two Lambs: one let him consume at Communion, and the other let him place in the tabernacle and keep until the day of the feast. All this let him do according to the rubric given for Great Thursday here, on page 385, in the note. On the day of the feast itself, after the Proskomedia, immediately before the beginning of the Divine Liturgy, after the censing of everything as usual by deacons (or by the Priest himself), the exposition of the Holy Mysteries takes place in the following way: the first deacon (who is on the right of the Priest) places the Gospel on the right side of the holy table, unlocks the artophorion and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, takes from the artophorion the pyx, all bend their knees, and he places it on the folded antimension; if there be a monstrance, then he unlocks the pyx, takes from it the Lamb, not touching it with his fingers, but holding by the stand on which it lies, places it into the groove of the monstrance, locks it well, then places the pyx into the artophorion, bows before it and, having locked the artophorion, places the monstrance, turned with face side to the people, on the antimension and steps aside a little to the right side. The Priest puts incense into the censer, blesses it, saying: "Blessed is our God", and censes with both hands the Holy Mysteries three times, bowing His head at each censing. Then, having taken upon Himself with the help of the second deacon the omophorion, approaches the holy table and, having bowed low, with the help of the first Deacon takes with both hands with the omophorion the monstrance and, having turned it with the reverse side to himself, turns his right side to the people and sings solemnly and majestically the beginning of the first strophe: "O saving Victim", and all people continue to sing the same strophe. And again the Priest – the beginning of the second strophe: "To the One God in Trinity", and all sing the rest. The Priest signs the people crosswise with the Holy Mysteries, then goes in a semicircle from the southern side to the northern and, having returned by the northern to the altar, places the monstrance on the antimension, having turned it with the help of the Deacon with face side to the people. Then, having stepped aside a little to the left, descends before the steps of the altar so as not to turn his back to the Holy Mysteries, kneels and, having put aside the omophorion and having censed again three times the Holy Mysteries, as at the beginning, waits, kneeling, until the Deacon, having approached the middle of the altar and bowed low, places the Holy Mysteries on the tabernacle. Then the Priest, having ascended the steps, begins the Liturgy from "Blessed is the Kingdom", "O Heavenly King" and the rest. During the Liturgy the sacred ministers never turn their backs to the Holy Mysteries, as our Sluzhebnyky prescribe: "When (the Priest), according to the ritual prescriptions, has to turn to the people, he should not turn from the middle of the altar, so as not to turn his back to the Body of Christ, but, having bowed low and stepped aside a little to the left side, from this side turns to the people and, having turned again to the altar, bows low to the Body of Christ, and then, when the Priest has to make a full turn, as at 'Always, now and ever', when he turns with the Holy Mysteries, then he does not make a full turn, so as not to turn his back to the Body of Christ"[^662]. Let us add also that when the Priest or deacon goes out before the iconostasis for censing, he does not cense from the middle, nor turns his back to the Holy Mysteries, but stands a little on the side, the Priest – from the side of the Theotokos, and the deacons: one – from the side of the Savior, and the other – of the Theotokos.

units.english_text: After the conclusion of the Prayer behind the Ambo the sacred ministers stand before the steps of the altar, and the first deacon ascends the steps and, having bowed low, takes down the Holy Mysteries from the tabernacle, places on the folded antimension and steps aside a little to his side. All kneel, and the Priest, having censed three times the Holy Mysteries and having taken upon himself the omophorion, ascends the steps, with the help of the Deacon takes with both hands the Holy Mysteries, turns to the people, as at the beginning of the Liturgy, and, having begun the troparion "Bread transubstantiated" or some other pious hymn, preceded by two deacons with censers, enters under the canopy and proceeds to the church doors to the sounds of bells and the procession from the church to the first altar begins, and the Choir and people continue to sing the troparion or something else. The order of the procession is such. In front goes the cross-bearer between two candle-bearers, then banner- and icon-bearers, then four girls with icons, after them the church brotherhood, two by two, with candles, choirs and all the clergy, two by two, with candles, according to their dignity: the nearest priests – in phelonia, and others – in epitrachelia, the last – the main priest with the Holy Mysteries, preceded by two deacons, who from the sides unceasingly cense, and candle-bearers surrounding the canopy. When the procession arrives at the first altar and stops near it, all the clergy divides into two wings, the canopy is placed opposite the altar, and the Priest with the Holy Mysteries ascends to the altar and, with the help of the Deacon, places the Holy Mysteries on the folded antimension; then, having bent his knees, censes them three times and, having risen, steps aside a little to the left and turns to the people. Then the Gospel-bearers approach the Priest, the Priest opens the Gospel at the place of the 1st reading, and the first Deacon exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy" etc., choir responds "Lord, have mercy" (3), priest sings: "Peace be to all"; second deacon: "Wisdom, Aright. Let us listen" etc., priest: "The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)" and, when the first Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend", the Priest reads the first Gospel (Matthew, Section 108. 17-30). After the conclusion of the reading he kisses its beginning and, having bent his knees before the Holy Mysteries, sings (if there is a custom) with other sacred ministers the first member of the supplicatory song *“Holy God”* three times and all people – the same three times. Then, having again censed the Holy Mysteries three times and risen, bows low, takes the Holy Mysteries with both hands and, having turned to the right to the people blesses them crosswise once (bishop – three times), saying quietly: "Save, O God, Thy people and bless Thine inheritance", and so, to the singing of the festal troparion or other hymn, the Priest enters under the canopy and the procession moves to the second altar, from it – to the third, then – to the fourth, and at each everything takes place exactly as at the first, only the members of the supplicatory song and the readings of the Gospels are changed, of which the second will be from Mark, Section 64.12-26; the third – from Luke, Section 108.7-22; the fourth – from John, Section 23.48-58. If there be several priests, they read the Gospels alternately. After this the procession returns to the church and the Priest, having placed the Holy Mysteries on the altar, kneels, censes them three times, rises and, having taken the Holy Mysteries and turned to the people, sings solemnly and majestically the verse of the Ambrosian hymn: "Save Thy people, O Lord" (3), and the people repeat the first and second time the same, and when the Priest sings it the third time and finishes with the words "and bless Thine inheritance" blessing the people once, then the people sing the further verses of this hymn, and the Priest, having turned with the northern side to the altar and placed the Holy Mysteries on it, descends before the steps, puts aside the omophorion, kneels and censes them three times. Then the right deacon approaches the Holy Mysteries, bows low, takes from the tabernacle the pyx and, having taken the Lamb from the monstrance, places it with the stand into the pyx, and places it into the tabernacle and, having again bowed, locks the tabernacle and places the Gospel on the antimension. If there be no deacon, then the Priest himself does all this. Then all rise, and the Choir sings "Blessed be the name of the Lord" and the rest of the Liturgy, as usual.

units.english_text: The temple rubrics used among us are of a double kind: some are borrowed from local Western Churches, which do not enter into the composition of our divine service, but are only added to it; others are natural to our divine service. Rubrics borrowed from Western Churches relate to the Holy Mysteries of the Eucharist, which are exposed on the holy table on the day of the temple feast and with which a procession takes place around the church. First, it befits us to provide the rubrics for the exposition and procession, and later – for the others.

units.english_text: On one of the days preceding the feast, the Priest shall consecrate two Lambs at the Liturgy: with one let him communicate, and the other, having placed [It] in the pyx [darokhranylnytsia], let him keep until the day of the feast. Let him do all this according to the rubric given for Great Thursday here, on [p. 385](Final_Dolnytsky_part4_triodion.md#great-thursday---divine-liturgy-and-consecration-of-the-lamb). When the very day of the feast comes, after the completion of the Proskomedia, immediately before the beginning of the Liturgy, the deacons (or the Priest himself) cense everything according to custom and the exposition of the Holy Mysteries takes place exactly as was noted for the feast of the Most Holy Eucharist here, on [p. 449](Final_Dolnytsky_part4_triodion.md#solemnity-of-the-most-holy-body-and-blood-of-christ-eucharist).

units.english_text: Before the beginning of Vespers, the Priest, dressed in all sacerdotal [vestments], and the Deacon – in all diaconal vestments, having come before the steps of the holy table, open the holy doors and the first deacon, having laid aside the Gospel to the right side, takes the Holy Mysteries from the tabernacle [kyvot] and places Them on the iliton; the Priest censes Them thrice over all, as at the beginning of the Liturgy, places Them on the skynia [exposition throne] on the folded iliton and, having placed the Gospel again in the middle of the holy table, exclaims: "Bless, Master," and the Priest, standing with the deacons at the holy table, begins: "Blessed is our God." Vespers is sung with an Entrance. The Priest departs from the holy table only at the Entrance, and the deacons – also at the litanies and after the prokimenon for the sermon, if there be one; then the Holy Mysteries are covered with a veil.

units.english_text: Before the dismissal of Vespers, all kneel, and the Deacon takes the Holy Gospel from the middle of the holy table and, having placed it on the right side, removes the Holy Mysteries from the skynia and places [Them] on the folded iliton. The Priest censes Them thrice with a bowing of the head and, having given away the censer, takes upon himself the omophorets [humeral veil], approaches the Holy Mysteries and, having bowed low, takes Them with both hands, with the help of the Deacon, turns right to the people, begins some pious hymn and goes out through the holy doors into the church; he enters under the baldachin and proceeds to the church doors, preceded by deacons with censers, who incessantly cense the Holy Mysteries from the sides; after them follow other priests in phelons, some – only in epitrachelia, with lighted candles in their hands, in two wings, likewise – the church brotherhood, afterwards – four girls with icons, banner-bearers and the cross-bearer. Under the sounds of bells, the procession goes out of the church and encircles it, beginning from its northern side, and returning from the southern side. When the Priest with the Holy Mysteries reaches the middle of the northern side, the procession stops, interrupts the singing, all kneel, and the Priest blesses all the present people with the Holy Mysteries four times, that is, first directly before himself, then – to the right side, then – behind and finally – to the left, saying each time in a quiet voice: "Save, O God, Thy people and bless Thine inheritance." Similarly it happens on the eastern, southern and western sides[^664]. After the blessing on the western side, the procession enters the church: first the Priest with the Holy Mysteries, other sacred ministers, then – the rest of the procession and the people. Then the Priest places the Holy Mysteries on the holy table, on the folded iliton, and, having laid aside the omophorets, kneels and censes the Holy Mysteries thrice. All kneel, and the Priest, together with other sacred ministers, sings the verses of the supplicatory hymn "Holy God." All the people repeat each of its verses. After the completion of the litiya, the Priest, having censed the Holy Mysteries thrice and having taken upon himself the omophorets, approaches the holy table and, having bowed low, takes the Holy Mysteries and, having turned right to the people, sings piously the verse of the hymn of St. Ambrose "Save Thy people, O Lord" twice, and the people repeat the same. The third time the Priest [sings]: "Save Thy people, O Lord, and bless Thine inheritance"; singing: "and bless," He blesses the people solemnly crosswise, making a half-turn from the right to the left side.

units.english_text: The feast of a temple saint, even if of a lower rank, exceeds even a feast of a saint with a Vigil, primarily in that, when it falls on a Sunday, it includes at Matins before the Canon the Prokimenon, the Gospel, and the Sunday Sticheron [after the Gospel], exactly as a Feast of the Theotokos; also, the Gospel Sticheron is transferred from the "Praises" to the end of Matins. Besides this, if it falls on a weekday, it excludes at the Liturgy the Apostle and Gospel of the day, which is then read on the day before the feast. Finally, the temple feast of a saint has its Apodosis, which takes place on the very day of the feast at Vespers for the following day, with an Entrance, as on a Feast of the Lord. In this Apodosis at "Lord, I have cried," there will be 6 stichera: 3 of the temple and 3 of the daily saint; Glory: of the temple; Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday [*Octoechos*] (Dogmatic) according to the tone of the Doxastikon. If the temple is of the Lord or of the Theotokos, then also Glory, Both now: of the temple. On Friday evening for Saturday, we always sing the Dogmatic of the tone that is being given away. After the Prokimenon – "Let us all say." Aposticha of the temple with its verses, Glory: of the temple, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday [*Octoechos*], according to the tone of the Doxastikon. If the temple is of the Lord or of the Theotokos, then Both now: of the temple. At the end: Troparion of the temple, Glory: Troparion of the daily saint, Glory, Both now: of the temple. Great Dismissal with the commemoration of the temple and the daily saint. At this Vespers, the service of the temple saint concludes; however, a temple saint does not have an Apodosis if the following day falls on a Sunday, or a Polyeleos saint

units.english_text: If the feast of a temple saint falls in the midst of a feast, that is, during the Forefeast, Afterfeast, or Apodosis of a feast – observe the rubric of a Saint with Vigil in the Afterfeast, whether on a Sunday or on a weekday here, on [pp. 104-105](Final_Dolnytsky_part2_general_rubrics.md#general-rubric-for-a-temple-saint-in-the-afterfeast)[^667], only on Sunday, at Matins, we sing the Prokimenon, Gospel and Sticheron of the temple; at the Praises – Glory: of the temple, and the Gospel Sticheron – after the dismissal of Matins[^668]

units.english_text: On the very day of the feast, after the Ambo [prayer], in our lands, a Blessing of Water usually takes place outside the church, to where a procession goes: in front – the cross-bearer, then – the censer-bearer, the Deacon with the Gospel, and the Priest with a hand cross. It befits the church servers to carry there also the boat with incense, the sprinkler with the holy water vessel, a glass [cup], and a towel, so that the cross may be wiped after immersing it in the water, as well as the hands of the Priest. After the dismissal of the Liturgy, the Polychronion is sung for the Ecumenical Pontiff, the Emperor, the Metropolitan, one's own Bishop, all present sacred ministers, and all people of the parish

After the 3rd Ode – Kontakion and Ikos of the *Triodion*, then – Sessional Hymn of the temple, Glory, Both now: of the *Triodion*; after the 6th – Kontakion and Ikos of the temple; after the 9th – Sunday Exaposteilarion, Glory: of the temple, Both now: of the *Triodion*. Katavasia of the season, only on Meatfare Sunday the Katavasia is of the *Triodion*. Stichera at the Praises – 8: 4 Sunday and 4 of the temple with its verses, Glory: of the temple, Both now: "Most Blessed"; however, on Meatfare and Cheesefare Sundays, after four stichera of the temple with their verses, we sing the Idiomelon sticheron of the *Triodion* with the verse "Arise, O Lord," Glory: the same, Both now: "Most Blessed"[^678]

units.english_text: On these days we sing the service of the temple just as of other great saints which fall during Great Lent; and where at Matins there will be no *Triodion* [Three-Odes], we sing the Canon of the Theotokos with the Heirmos on 6 and of the temple on 8. Katavasia of the Theotokos. And where we sing the *Triodion* [Three-Odes], we take the Canon of the temple on 6 and of the *Triodion* according to its order (on 8), and at the end – Heirmos of the *Triodion*[^685].

units.english_text: We sing the service of the temple in the evening, and the stichera as indicated for the Theologian or St. George with Mid-Pentecost. On Pentecost Sunday, at Great Vespers – "Entrance," Great Prokimenon *“Who is so great a God”*; Readings (readings – 3) are of the temple and everything else with the kneeling prayers. At the Litiya: stichera of the temple, if there be any, Glory: of the temple, Both now: of the feast. Aposticha of the feast with its stichera; the rest of the service in the evening and in the morning is sung just as for the Theologian on Mid-Pentecost[^690].

units.english_text: The general Katavasia of the Theotokos is "I will open," however, on the Sundays of the Prodigal, Meatfare, Cheesefare, on the 1st and 3rd of Lent, on the Saturday of Lazarus, on Palm Sunday and in Passion Week there will be the Katavasia of the *Triodion* of the Canon of the day. Only during the period of the Katavasia of the Meeting, that is from January 15 to February 9, there will be the Katavasia of the feast, with the exception of Meatfare Sunday, for which the Slavonic rubrics provide the Katavasia of the *Triodion* (obviously, besides the very day of the feast)[^693].

units.english_text: At the top of the table, that is, in its 1st transverse row, all 35 Paschal keys are indicated, under each of which extends a row, or column, of Sundays of the whole year, with the indication of the day of the month within which these Sundays fall, and their dates or names. The names of the months are given outside the column, on the left side, and separated from one another by transverse step-like lines; the day of the month is given in the column, and the number or name of the Sunday – outside the column, on the right side of the table

units.english_text: In the five rows that are between the Publican and the Paschal keys, are indicated all 35 Sundays that may fall between Theophany and the Publican, that is, the Sunday after Theophany and the four last ordinary ones (29th, 30th, 31st and 32nd). However, since not all these Sundays will always take place, the explanation of which we gave on [p. 144](Final_Dolnytsky_part3_menaion.md#sunday-of-the-holy-ancestors-forefathers) (for this depends on whether Pascha falls earlier or later), between these five Sundays some places may be unfilled, and this means that then the Sundays corresponding to them, indicated on the right side of the table, will not take place. For example, under the Paschal key "A" all places are unfilled; this means that none of these 5 Sundays will be taken, but immediately after Theophany – the *Triodion

units.english_text: According to the rubric of the Greek *Euchologion*, the holy doors are opened only εις την αρχήν του μεγάλου Εσπερινού, οτε θυμια μονός ο Ιερεύς, εις τας εισόδους πασάς, ήγουν των Εσπερινών και της Λειτουργίας, και του αγίου Ευαγγελίου. Ωσαύτως ανοίγεται και από του Μετά φόβου... μέχρι της συμπληρώσεως της θείας Λειτουργίας.

units.english_text: The curtain, according to the present custom of Athonite monasteries, at the Liturgy, after the completion of the Proskomedia, is drawn open, and at the "Great Entrance" is drawn shut; at "Especially" it is drawn open, and at "And grant that with one mouth" it is drawn shut; at "With fear" it is drawn open and so remains until the conclusion of the Liturgy[^751]. According to the former custom of the Athonite Mountain, when one priest serves, that is without a Deacon, the curtain is drawn shut at the "Great Entrance" and is not drawn open until the end of communion. Besides this, it remains drawn open at Vespers and at Matins from the 1st Hour and at the Moleben. When the Hours are celebrated without Liturgy, it is drawn open for the reading of the Apostle and drawn shut after the dismissal of the "Typika"[^752].
